The wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was rushed to the hospital after being shot at the couple's home in Virginia, according to ESPN.

Mia Bieniemy, 57, was shot Sunday night, ESPN reported, citing unnamed sources. Police in Loudoun County, Virginia, told the publication that a victim was being treated for “serious injuries” but did not provide the person's name.

“The club is aware of the incident involving Eric Bieniemy’s family,” the Chiefs said in a statement.

“Out of respect for their privacy, we won’t have a comment at this time. Our thoughts and prayers are with them.”

open image in gallery Bieniemy returned to the Chiefs as offensive coordinator in 2026 ( Getty Images )

Eric Bieniemy was with the team at training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri, on Sunday.

He is beginning his second stint as the Chiefs' offensive coordinator, a role he served in from 2018-22.

Bieniemy was the Chicago Bears running backs coach last season.

News.title: Man who escaped prison van told he may never be released after ‘bestial’ rape of girl
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A rapist who escaped from a prison van has been told he may never be released from prison.

Aaron Strachan, 21, stalked, abducted and raped the 15-year-old in the York Place area of Edinburgh on May 25 last year.

On the same day he also stabbed a man in an “unprovoked” attack in the South Bridge area and attacked another man with a hammer in High Riggs on May 28.

Strachan had been due to be sentenced earlier this year but escaped while being led from the Court of Session to a prison van following a hearing in January.

A major police search was launched and he was recaptured in the city a few hours later.

open image in gallery Aaron Strachan, in a picture dating from 2019, was jailed at the High Court in Edinburgh ( Police Scotland )

The 21-year-old pleaded guilty to the rape and two assaults on December 4 2025, and on Monday pleaded guilty to attempting to defeat the ends of justice.

At the High Court in Edinburgh on Monday, Judge Michael O’Grady KC imposed an order for lifelong restriction on Strachan with a minimum period of five years in custody, telling him he may never be released.

Strachan first approached the 15-year-old girl as she waited at a bus stop in Edinburgh city centre in the early hours of May 25.

After feeling uneasy she walked away towards Princes Street, and Strachan was caught on CCTV following her, with his face covered by a balaclava.

He then ran towards the girl as she sat at a second bus stop, threatening to harm her while brandishing a knife.

After seizing her by the shoulders he forcibly led her to the basement on York Place, where he blocked the door with wooden pallets before raping her.

Judge O’Grady told Strachan his actions were “the stuff of nightmares for every woman and every young girl, and every parent who waits at home for their child to return home safely”.

“The word predatory is perhaps overused in these courts, but it is an inescapable adjective to describe this truly bestial crime,” he said.

“You left your lair and went out hunting for a vulnerable victim.

“Finding one, you stalked her, threatened her at knifepoint and took her to a dingy basement and raped her.”

Describing the other two attacks, he told Strachan they had been “unprovoked” and carried out on “virtual strangers”.

He said the attack on May 25 – the same day as the rape – had left his victim with two knife wounds to his right hand.

open image in gallery Strachan escaped while being led from the Court of Session (pictured) to a prison van following a hearing in January ( PA Archive )

In the later attack, the judge told Strachan he had struck his victim on the head with a metal hammer, leaving him “semi-conscious” on the ground and suffering seizures.

The man was later found to have a suffered a fractured skull and bleeding on the brain, with the judge saying the consequences of the attack for the man had been “catastrophic”.

The judge also laid out Strachan’s “concerning” criminal record, telling him he had appeared in court on 18 previous occasions in relation to 38 separate charges, eight of which involved possession of weapons.

The judge told Strachan he was “entirely satisfied” he met the criteria for an order for lifelong restriction order – an indeterminate sentence that means an offender is not released until deemed to no longer pose a risk to the public.

The judge told him: “You are likely to remain in prison for many years, if indeed you are ever released.”

Strachan, who remained handcuffed to security officers throughout the hearing, showed no reaction as the sentence was handed down.

Earlier, Strachan’s lawyer Simon Collins told the court his client’s actions were “extremely serious offences”.

“I accept that, and Aaron Strachan accepts that,” Mr Collins told the court.

“The inevitable outcome of the offences of this seriousness is that he is facing an extremely lengthy period in custody.”

The court was also shown CCTV footage of the moment Strachan slipped his cuffs and ran off while being led from the Court of Session to a waiting prison van.

The footage shows Strachan, dressed in a red top, walking between two guards towards the van, before “yanking” his hand free and sprinting away in the direction of the Royal Mile.

Mr Collins told the court it had been “a moment of impulsiveness” on Strachan’s part, saying his client had noticed the handcuffs linking him to a security guard were “not tight enough to prevent him from removing his hand”.

Faye Cook, procurator fiscal for High Court sexual offences, said: “Aaron Strachan’s actions in abducting his victim before raping her were calculated, predatory and caused profound harm.

“Although this type of stranger offending is rare, this conviction reflects the gravity of his crimes and the commitment of prosecutors and police to bring him to justice.

Detective Inspector Gillian Wells, from Edinburgh’s Sex Offender Policing Unit, said: “This was a particularly harrowing attack which was carried out in the busy city centre area and had a profound effect on the young victim.

“I hope this sentence brings her some sense of closure.

“The other assaults also demonstrate what a violent individual Strachan is, with no consideration of the consequences of his actions. “

Jakob Ingebrigtsen appears set to compete at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham as the Norwegian nears a return from a long injury lay-off.

The Norwegian has not featured in a competitive race in 2026 after undergoing surgery earlier in the year on an Achilles issue that also heavily impacted his 2025 season.

But Ingebrigtsen appears set to target more continental success in August having seemingly confirmed his participation in a social media post.

The 25-year-old has won double gold in the 1500m and 5000m at each of the last three European Championships.

“I’ve heard Birmingham is nice this time of year…” Ingebrigtsen said on Instagram, teasing his return.

Struggling with that Achilles strain, the two-time Olympic champion was below his best at the World Championships in Tokyo last year as he finished only 10th in the 5000m and failed to advance from the first round of the 1500m.

Ingebrigtsen has done the double in Berlin, Munich and Rome and is thus far unbeaten at the Euros.

The 2026 edition begins in Birmingham on 10 August, and while Ingebrigtsen is perhaps likelier to enter the 5000m, he could yet renew his rivalry over the shorter distance with Josh Kerr.

The Scot is still chasing a first European title but recently broke the mile world record in London – though would face a tight turnaround before the event from the Commonwealth Games.

Keely Hodgkinson is among the British stars set to be in action on home soil next month.

News.content:
Suspect in custody after three killed in mass shooting at popular food festival

A 2-year-old boy is among the four people who were injured in a mass shooting that took place at a popular Seattle food festival Sunday.

Gunfire rang out at the annual Bite of Seattle event around 6 p.m. local time, sending crowds of people running for safety. At least three people were killed in the shooting – two were declared deceased at the scene while another succumbed to their injuries at a local hospital.

Police have apprehended one suspect, who surrendered at the scene, and are currently searching for a second, Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said.

“There were two people who we believe were shooting at each other,” he said.

As of Monday morning, two adults who were rushed to Harborview Medical Center with injuries had been discharged while the 2-year-old was in ‘satisfactory’ condition and still being cared for, Harborview Medical Center spokesperson Susan Gregg told The Seattle Times.

No details have yet been released about those involved in the attack.

Cracker Barrel said Monday that CEO Julie Felss Masino will step down after a turbulent year marked by a controversial rebranding effort that drew conservative backlash and weighed on the company’s financial performance.

The popular restaurant chain announced that David Deno, the former CEO of Bloomin' Brands — the parent company of Outback Steakhouse — will succeed Felss Masino.

“Cracker Barrel is a truly iconic American brand, defined by its unique combination of warm country hospitality, timeless appeal, and deep connection with guests across generations,” Deno said in a news release. “I am honored to lead the Cracker Barrel team and look forward to unlocking the full potential of this remarkable brand.”

The leadership change comes on the heels of a $700 million rebranding effort last year that gave some restaurants a more modern look. But the defining flashpoint arrived on August 19, when the company unveiled a new logo. The redesign replaced an image of a man known as ‘Old Timer’ leaning on a barrel with a pared down logo depicting just the company’s name.

The update sparked a wave of backlash from prominent MAGA figures, who accused the company of going “woke” and abandoning a nostalgic symbol in favor of a more sterile logo.

open image in gallery Cracker Barrel said that CEO Julie Felss Masino will step down after a turbulent year marked by a controversial rebranding effort that drew backlash from President Trump ( REUTERS )

Rep. Byron Donalds, a Florida Republican, wrote on X, “Their logo was iconic and their unique restaurants were a fixture of American culture. No one asked for this woke rebrand. It’s time to Make Cracker Barrel Great Again.”

Even President Donald Trump weighed in, writing on Truth Social on August 25: “Cracker Barrel should go back to the old logo, admit a mistake based on customer response (the ultimate Poll), and manage the company better than ever before.” The White House, echoing the president’s remarks, wrote on X: ‘Go woke, go broke.’

The controversy drove a sharp drop in the company’s stock, erasing $94 million in market value in one day.

open image in gallery The new logo, unveiled on August 19, did not include the iconic ‘Old Timer’ leaning over a barrel ( Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

open image in gallery The company announced it would revert back to the old logo on August 26. ‘We said we would listen, and we have,’ Cracker Barrel said in a statement ( Getty )

On August 26, the company, headquartered in Tennessee, announced it would revert back to the old logo.

“We thank our guests for sharing your voices and love for Cracker Barrel,” the company said in a statement. “We said we would listen, and we have. Our new logo is going away and our ‘Old Timer’ will remain.’

Trump praised the decision, writing on Truth Social: "All of your fans very much appreciate it,” and shares of the restaurant operator rose after the reversal was announced.

Felss Masino said in October that the short-lived rebrand was supposed to be functional, not ideological. She believed the new logo would be easier to see on billboards, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The company, which later nixed plans to remodel 660 restaurants, appears to have weathered the storm successfully. Last month, it reported third-quarter profit of $42.8 million, up from $12.6 million a year earlier, according to the Journal.

Last week, Cracker Barrel announced it was closing all locations of its sister brand, Maple Street Biscuit Company.

I love travelling by train: no depressing airports, no hidden luggage charges and much more legroom. But it’s not just the practical stuff. There’s also the sense of freedom, possibility and immersion you only get on the rails, letting the journey become part of the holiday, not a hurdle to cross before you get there. All of which means that I’m a sucker for a sleeper train.

Many of Europe’s classic sleeper routes were axed during the 2010s and the pandemic. But in the last few years, there’s been talk of a night train renaissance: new routes, new operators and a dawning sense that a way of getting from A to B previously considered passé might just be the future of travel.

Although state railway bureaucracy doesn’t make it easy, the map of sleeper trains across Europe keeps expanding. And now there’s a new link that makes it simpler to travel flight-free from the UK to one of the great cities of northern Europe: Hamburg.

open image in gallery A new, direct overnight service from Brussels to Hamburg has just been launched by European Sleeper ( European Sleeper )

Germany’s second-biggest city, with a population significantly larger than Birmingham, Hamburg has centuries of seafaring history – and some legendary nightlife in the old sailor-town of St Pauli. I’ve wanted to visit for years, but getting there without flying involved a whole day of train-hopping, with multiple changes. Until now.

A new, direct overnight service from Brussels to Hamburg has just been launched by European Sleeper, a plucky, independent Dutch-Belgian rail company. It runs three times a week, with just one easy change of trains between London and Hamburg. This means you can leave London in the afternoon and arrive in Hamburg early the next morning, doing much of your travelling while you’re asleep. I didn’t need any more persuading to hop aboard the first ever eastbound voyage of the “Good Night Train” to Germany’s northern metropolis.

Starting in London, the first step is Eurostar, ever the gateway to European adventures. I’m always amazed at how short the cross-channel journey is. One minute you’re gazing over the industrial estates of the Thames Estuary, the next you’re surrounded by the redbrick houses and bulbous water towers of Belgium’s capital.

Brussels is in the midst of overturning its drab reputation with a new wave of genuinely cool cultural openings, such as the upcoming Kanal offshoot of Paris’s Pompidou Centre. Unfortunately, there isn’t time to gallery-hop – I’ve got just a couple of hours for a veggie couscous at a North African friterie and a stroll around the multicultural Marolles neighbourhood, before it’s time to hop the overnight train to Germany.

No “arrive two hours early for your flight” here: I rock up to the platform five minutes before the train pulls in. There’s a buzz among the waiting passengers that you never get at an airport gate. We’ve all chosen the adventurous over the obvious, and there’s a real sense of community among the student backpackers, young families, hip-looking groups of friends and solo travellers of all ages.

The train pulls in; there’s a shuffle on the platform and some polite, multilingual squeezing-past in the train corridors as everyone hops aboard and finds where they’ll be sleeping for the night. Across its ten carriages, this train can carry nearly 400 passengers – roughly two planes’ worth.

I’m booked into a couchette cabin: the classic sleeper train set-up, with five fairly basic bunks accessed via a ladder. I’ve booked the very top bunk, which is harder to climb up to, but darker, more private and with better storage space. My return ticket cost around €230 (£195), plus the price of the Eurostar. Yes, it’s more expensive than a budget flight, but a bit of a bargain once you realise you’re saving on two nights’ accommodation.

open image in gallery James stayed in a couchette cabin, but there are a range of sleeper options ( James Manning )



There are also more luxurious cabin with proper beds and duvets, sleeping up to three people (and with the option to book out the whole room for just one or two travellers). At the opposite end of the scale is the budget carriage where you kip in your seat, populated mostly by the aforementioned student backpackers.

My couchette cabin is full of different nationalities: French, Belgian, German, me. There are night-train veterans like Charles, from Toulouse. He’s on his way from Paris to Berlin, as part of an Interrail adventure that’ll take him via the Baltics all the way to Narvik, Europe’s most northerly rail station outside Russia, high up in Norway’s Arctic Circle. Then there are first-timers, like Malte, a Hamburger on his way home from Paris. He thought he’d give the sleeper train a try, and is surprised to hear that a week ago, this journey wouldn’t even have been possible.

We’re moving. The sun sets and the Belgian countryside whips by outside. After a final evening stop at Liege’s soaring Guillemins station, it’s lights off.

It is worth clarifying at this point that the European Sleeper’s “Good Night Train” is not the Orient Express. Finding suitable carriages is one of the biggest challenges for any company wanting to launch night train routes, and the train I’m riding is decidedly retro. The corridors are dotted with lights and dials that look something from a Cold War submarine, and the toilets are prone to getting blocked (hence the repeated reminders to not flush paper towels). The air conditioning leaves a lot to be desired, though it’s a blast (literally) to rattle along with the carriage window open. There’s a sort of Wes Anderson charm to the old-school atmosphere, but it’s best not to expect luxury.

open image in gallery Hamburg is Europe’s third biggest port ( Getty/iStock )

Still, I get a surprisingly decent night’s rest, woken only sporadically by metallic clanks and the rattle of other trains passing. The swaying of the train is mostly soothing – so much so that I’m woken a few times by a sudden stillness as we pull into a siding.

But I soon drift off again, and when I next wake, I get an almost magical surprise. It’s 6am, the cabin is light and the train has come to rest at Platform 5 of Hamburg Harburg station. I grab my bags, trying not to wake my fellow passengers (most of whom are still dozing, bound for Berlin), and hop down into a brand new city.

After coffee at the Elbgold roastery and a morning dip and shower at the stunning, neo-gothic Kaifubad pool complex, I spend a colourful day running around Hamburg. I climb a former Nazi bunker that’s recently been converted into a panoramic roof garden. I wander the buzzy, graffiti-decked streets of Schanzenviertel and Karolinenviertel and the peaceful paths of the Planten un Blomen botanical garden. I eat superbly: Austrian dumplings at Marend, pizza alla Norma at vibey Tazzi, and a pastel de nata in the Portuguese Quarter that could have come fresh from Lisbon.

As befits a port city (Europe’s third largest, in fact), Hamburg is an open-minded place with a thriving counterculture. The skull-and-crossbones symbol of anti-fascist football heroes FC St Pauli is everywhere, and venues like the anarchist art squat Rote Flora, the art-filled micro-neighbourhood Gängeviertel and the punk record shop Fischkopp provide a support system for the kind of alternative, creative communities that are increasingly being squeezed out of British cities.

open image in gallery The transformed Second World War bunker in the heart of the city ( Getty Images / iStockPhoto )



St Pauli’s red-light district (where The Beatles famously honed their rock ’n’ roll chops) and its waterfront are undeniably pretty touristy. But perhaps the biggest surprise: I hardly overhear anyone speaking English all day.

Could that change? Hamburg is ripe for discovery by UK travellers: it’s a creative, vibrant city with a distinctive northern character that’s very different from what you’ll find in Berlin or Munich.

And for train fans, there’s one extra draw: Hamburg is a vital link to the north. From here, direct trains (including sleepers) run all the way to Copenhagen, Stockholm and Malmo. From 2028, that list will also include Oslo and Gothenburg.

So the new European Sleeper link doesn’t just make it much simpler to get from London to an underrated city-break destination – it also unlocks a whole world of flight-free Scandinavian adventures. Who needs planes, anyway?

How to do it

Take a Eurostar from London St Pancras to Brussels-Midi (from £39 one-way), then a European Sleeper to Hamburg (from £25 one-way for a seat, or £60 for a couchette). Total travel time is from 12 hours.

Where to stay

If you’re not boarding the sleeper train straight home again, check in to Side Design Hotel Hamburg. It’s halfway between the city centre and hip Schanzenviertel, with easy U-Bahn connections across the city, and has a pool, sauna and hot tub – plus a sleek roof terrace. Rooms cost from £160 a night.

James travelled as a guest of Eurostar

News.title: Funeral director who gave families wrong ashes and kept bodies for months apologises outside court
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Families who were given the wrong ashes and had their deceased loved ones kept for months by a funeral director have said they are “appalled” by his apology.

Robert Bush, 48, is due to be sentenced after he kept the bodies of 31 people, including a stillborn baby, at his site in Hull.

An investigation discovered 100 sets of ashes at Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, some with name labels and letters attached to the box.

Upon arriving in court wearing a face covering, Bush apologised to the affected families and told BBC reporters: “I’m sorry, yes.”

According to the broadcaster, he added: “I’ve written to the court. There is a letter submitted to the court.”

open image in gallery People demonstrate outside Hull Crown Court ahead of Bush’s sentencing ( PA )

However, his apology was poorly received by the families of those affected, who said they were “appalled” that he had apologised to journalists but not to them.

Hull Crown Court heard that Bush had mistreated hundreds of families on an “almost industrial scale” and that his offending had affected “young and old alike”.

Bush was arrested after police were contacted by someone with access to the site in March 2024, expressing concerns over “care of the deceased” at the business.

Patrick Moore, a former casual employee at Legacy who made the discovery, described the premises as “something from a horror scene”.

Officers discovered 31 bodies that should have been cremated months earlier and half a tonne of human ashes, as well as a human foetus in a bag.

Gasps were heard in court from family members as details of the scene were described in court.

Upon being arrested at Heathrow airport, Bush told police: “I’ve f***** it all up, everything, my whole world.”

Mr Paxton said Bush told officers he had debts of around £90,000.

open image in gallery Funeral director Robert Bush was arrested after police received a report voicing concerns about his business ( Humberside Police )

Police found that many families of the deceased found at Legacy had already been given ashes by Bush, revealing a widespread practice of him giving grieving relatives the wrong ashes.

In her victim impact statement, Karen King said she feels “violated” after discovering she had been wearing “some unknown person’s ashes” in a locket around her neck after the death of her father. She had also given Bush a bottle of port for “taking care” of her father, with the discovery of his actions causing her to have an “emotional breakdown”.

In total, there were 254 victims of Bush’s crimes, with all the charges dating from a period between May 2012 and 6 March 2024.

Investigators also learned that Bush had committed fraudulent trading in relation to funeral plans, where he would take payment for the plans but not pass any of the money on to the financial institutions that would hold it for when the funeral was required.

He also stole from charities by failing to pass on donations collected at funerals.

In one impact statement, David Gorbutt questioned why there is no regulation of the funeral industry.

Mr Gorbutt, whose wife Susan’s body was found at Legacy, said: “Those responsible for this atrocious breach of trust seem to work in an industry that is – hopefully, was – totally unregulated.

“Who knew that was the case? Certainly not me.

“It is hard to believe a person needs more permits to sell burgers than to deal with the dead.”

In his first police interview, Bush said he had developed a cash-flow problem because “people did not always pay,” and had debts of about £90,000.

He said he struggled with maintaining the payments for the leases, and believed there were about 30 bodies at the Hessle Road site, with five to six of them “recent” and waiting to be cremated.

The court heard that between March 2017 and April 2024, more that £3 million was paid into his business and personal accounts but the turnover reported to HMRC in these years does not reflect this.

During this time, Bush’s “profligate personal spending” and transfers to his wife accounted for over £879,000, Mr Paxton said.

In April, Bush pleaded guilty to 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial, and theft from 12 charities including the Salvation Army and Macmillan Cancer Support.

He had already admitted 30 counts of fraud by false representation relating to bodies found at the site, and four “foetus allegations” of fraud, where he presented ashes to women falsely saying that they were “the remains of their unborn”.

Bush also pleaded guilty to a further charge of fraud, covering the ashes of 57 people between 2017 and 2024, and one of fraudulent trading relating to funeral plans between 2012 and 2024.

The sentencing at Hull Crown Court is listed for five days, and is expected to hear from more than 100 victims.

Bush, formerly of Kirk Ella in East Yorkshire, but now of Otley in West Yorkshire, is on conditional bail.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.title: Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe
News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

Kick-off is at 12.30pm.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko injury update after Man Utd striker missed first two pre-season friendlies with shin problem
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED striker Benjamin Sesko is on schedule to return from a shin injury before the new season starts.

Sesko, 23, missed United’s first two pre-season friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg as he continues to follow a rehabilitation program.



Carrington sources say Sesko’s recovery is going to plan and he was never scheduled to participate in the opening friendlies.

Sesko was already nursing a shin injury that he aggravated in the 3-2 win against Liverpool on May 3.



United were vague about the extent of the injury at the time and the final three games of last season that Sesko sat out are set to be the only ones he misses.

The Slovenia international started outdoor training last week and has a chance of being involved against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday.

Sesko is likely to start against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on August 8 and United fly from Sweden to Dublin for a six-day training camp.

United play Leeds United at Croke Park on August 12, their penultimate friendly before they start the Premier League season against Hull City on August 22.

Sesko’s absence allowed Joshua Zirkzee to start against Wrexham and Rosenborg, despite United’s preference to sell him.

A sale is a long shot as United would require around £21million to avoid a loss on Zirkzee, who arrived for £36.5m in July 2024.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Zirkzee, 25, has generated interest from a number of Italian clubs during his time at United and a loan return to Serie A remains likely.

United want to sign a new striker to support Sesko but denied there had been any contact with Danny Welbeck before Chelsea registered their interest in the Brighton forward.

Welbeck scored 14 goals for Brighton last term and has always been open to a possible homecoming at United.

But Chelsea have moved for the 35-year-old, who is out of contract at Brighton next year.

The 26-year-old has been relaxing at a luxury resort in Montego Bay, Jamaica, with partner Virginia Fonseca.



However, Vinicius did give the pair a stressful experience after he was allowed to drive a golf cart through the hotel complex.

Other guests and staff helped the group push the cart back onto the path in the hilarious episode.

Virginia later shared the footage to her Instagram story and joked about his driving ability.

She wrote in the caption: “Who feels safe with Vini Jr driving?”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The couple previously enjoyed some time on a mega yacht in Sardinia with friends and family this month after Brazil were knocked out of the World Cup by Norway.

Sports.title: Chelsea targeting shock move for ex-Arsenal & Man Utd star Danny Welbeck, 35, in huge steer away from transfer policy
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are in talks with Brighton over a shock deal to sign striker Danny Welbeck.

New Blues boss Xabi Alonso is keen to add experience to his side this summer.



Welbeck, 35, scored 13 goals in 37 appearances for the Seagulls last season.

Chelsea have a number of strikers on their books already, with Liam Delap, Joao Pedro and Marc Guiu on their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia.



Nicolas Jackson is due to join up with the squad in Hong Kong after his holiday.

Jackson, however, is a target for Aston Villa with Chelsea valuing him at £65million.

Emmanuel Emegha has also joined from sister club Strasbourg this summer.

Former Manchester United and Arsenal marksman Welbeck enjoyed a stellar season for the Seagulls last term, coming close to an England recall.

Alonso has identified a need for more experienced players to create a stronger mentality within the club.

That was evidenced by a failed move for Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, who won the German title under Alonso.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Chelsea’s interest in Welbeck comes after the former Real Madrid chief admitted to expecting more arrivals before the transfer window slams shut.

Alonso said: “We have to be ready. The market is open for a few weeks.

“We need to be aware of different positions, different situations, so for sure, we have a plan, an idea, and we need to assess in the right moments.

“We can’t say what’s going to happen but some things might happen.



“We need to know that probably there will still be some movements. We need to be flexible and quick to act.

“The main thing is that we have a clear idea, a clear plan that we have built. Probably it will change until the last day of the market being open.

“We want to build a competitive team. We are in that process. We have great quality, great talent, and we need to know what it takes to compete in the Premier League.

“We want a squad with the right balance between quality and mentality.”

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer blow as Real Madrid still want Vinicius Jr to stay even after their £100m move for Yan Diomande
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’S pursuit of Vinicius Junior will not become any easier if Real Madrid sign Yan Diomande.

Real are closing in on a deal worth over £100million to sign Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer.



But even if the 19-year-old winger arrives at the Bernabeu, Real Madrid are expected to maintain their stance that they want to keep Vinicius Jr.

Arsenal are exploring a deal to sign Vinicius, who currently has just one year remaining on his deal at the Bernabeu.



Los Blancos have opened new talks to tie the Brazilian superstar down to a new long-term contract this week, but are yet to make a breakthrough in negotiations.

New boss Jose Mourinho also wants to keep hold of all of his star players this summer, however if no agreement is reached Madrid would want to avoid losing Vinicius on a free transfer next year.

The LaLiga club’s move for Diomande is understood to have no bearing on their stance that they wish to keep Vinicius.

And Diomande actually played the majority of his games for Leipzig last season on the right wing, the opposite flank to Vinicius.

Arsenal are closely monitoring Vinicius’ situation as talks over a new deal continue this week.

Despite the 26-year-old earning an eye-watering £400,000-per-week at the Bernabeu, Arsenal are confident they can meet his wage demands if a deal does materialise.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Any contract would make him Arsenal’s highest paid player ever.

Mikel Arteta is hoping to strengthen his front line further having already brought in Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge last week in a £34m deal.

The Gunners have already missed out on signing top target Morgan Rogers, who was swiped from underneath their noses by rivals Chelsea in a record £117m transfer.

Arsenal are still in for Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes, too.



The Toon captain has told club chiefs he would like to sign for Arsenal, but Newcastle bosses are keen to keep hold of their midfield maestro after already losing Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Sports.title: Troy Deeney names top 10 Premier League strikers ever… but leaves out ‘freak’ Erling Haaland with ‘a long way to go’
Sports.content:
TROY DEENEY reckons Erling Haaland has NOT yet cracked the 10 greatest Premier League strikers of all time.

Former Watford centre-forward Deeney admits Haaland is a “freak” but insists he “still has a long way to go”.



The Manchester City striker, 26, has netted 112 times in 132 league games, won the treble in 2023, and is by far the quickest player to reach a century of Prem goals.

But Deeney believes he has not yet done enough to oust the likes of Jermain Defoe or Robbie Fowler from his top 10.



He told talkSPORT: “He is a freak… I also think there’s still a long way to go.

“Haaland’s not in there, not yet, no. A lot of it for me is about feeling as well, what players made you feel when you watched them.”

Deeney added: “I think this season is going to be really interesting.

“The seasons he’s been at City, they have been unbelievable anyway and he’s been a piece to that, an additional piece. It’ll be interesting now they’re not favourites to win it.

“Can he carry the team a little bit? I’d like to see him drag this team forward.

“When he played against Arsenal, against Gabriel, I was like ‘wow’. He dragged the team to win that game, I’d like to see that more.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Deeney put Thierry Henry at the top of his list, followed by Wayne Rooney, Alan Shearer and Andy Cole.

Harry Kane, Sergio Aguero, Luis Suarez, Fowler and Defoe followed from five to nine in no particular order.



That left a tenth spot vacant, but Deeney still thinks Haaland needs to show more.

He said: “Henry, you watched him and you were like ‘wow’, you’d never seen anyone that quick, he had that finish into the bottom corner.

“Rooney, as a kid, he was one of the best players I’d ever seen, he could do it all.

“Shearer, it’s obviously goals.

“Cole is the most disrespected striker in Premier League history. He’s never in anybody else’s top 10. He scored over 180 goals.



“Defoe did it for so many years, Aguero was unbelievable.”

Sports.title: Abandoned UK stadium that hosted FA Cup finals set to be revived with £130million
Sports.content:
Abandoned UK stadium that hosted FA Cup finals set to be revived with £130million

A legendary stadium that has housed the likes of Usain Bolt is set to undergo significant redevelopment

View 3 Images Crystal Palace National Sports Centre is set to be restored to its former glory (Image: Jam Press/GLA)

The Crystal Palace National Sports Centre is set to open its doors once again thanks to a £130million redevelopment. The iconic stadium, located in south London, shut in November 2022 due to safety concerns and has largely been abandoned.

‌



However, plans to restore the ground - which had hosted the FA Cup final between 1895 and 1914 - to its former glory drawn up by the Greater London Authority and London mayor Sir Sadiq Khan are set to be approved by Bromley Council.

‌



Regarding the redevelopment plans, a Sport England spokesperson said: "The Crystal Palace National Sports Centre is tired and dated, and in desperate need of investment and modernisation in order to make it inclusive and accessible to all sections of the local community and to bring it into the 21st century, as well as to set in sound financial footing for the future."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist READ MORE :

Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts READ MORE :

The 15,500-seater stadium, which can be increased to 24,000 through temporary seating, has previously hosted international athletics and concerts featuring the likes of Coldplay and Bruce Springsteen.

Those in charge of the redevelopment want work to be complete by 2029, with full stadium renovation hoping to be done a year later. The seismic work expected to be done to transform the stadium could mark the return of the biggest athletic events to south London.

‌



View 3 Images London mayor Sadiq Khan and the Bromley Council are set to approve plans to revive it (Image: Jam Press/GLA)

The venue previously hosted Usain Bolt at the venue in 2009, just a year after the Jamaican icon become a double Olympic champion at the Beijing Games. The potential hosting of Diamond League meetings would allow Olympic 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson to compete at yet another stadium in her home country.

Among the plans to regenerate the centre is increasing the size of the gym, creating new spaces for sporting clubs and 3x3 basketball courts. The construction of a six-court padel centre has also been proposed, as well as five-a-side football pitches and a 200-metre running track.

‌



View 3 Images The 35,000-seater ground is set to be restored (Image: Jam Press/GLA)

The inclusion of a full-size artificial multi-sports pitch has been planned for on top of an outdoor gym and cafe. The ambitious plans aren't to everyone's tastes though, with some local residents making their displeasure heard.

According to the BBC, Bromley Council have received word from 390 people in favour of the redevelopment, with 406 people objecting to the plans.

Sports.content:

Meanwhile, according to the Daily Mail, Liverpool are working to reach an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over Bradley Barcola amid escalating valuations. Sports.title: Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update

Vinicius Jr has a clear desire that Arsenal can fulfil if he seals a remarkable transfer from Real Madrid

View 2 Images Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr is Arsenal's dream signing this summer (Image: (Photo by Antonio Pozo / Pressinphoto / Icon Sport))

Arsenal can help Vinicius Jr get his wish of wanting to be appreciated if he joins the club from Real Madrid. The 25-year-old emerged as a concrete target for the Gunners after Chelsea swooped in to sign Morgan Rogers for a stunning £117million.

‌



Though Arsenal were financially capable of meeting that amount, they had a clear valuation of Rogers that was exceeded by their London rivals. More funds would almost certainly be allocated to Vinicius if a deal became possible with his contract set to expire next summer.

‌



Attempts have been made by Real over the last 12 months to agree an extension and BBC Sport have claimed fresh talks were opened on Monday but there is yet to be a breakthrough. Their report has stated that while he open to staying and signing fresh terms, he wants to feel loved at whichever club he plays for.

‌



The 4 transfers Arsenal must complete for Mikel Arteta to win another Premier League title READ MORE :

Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star READ MORE :

If he made the move to Emirates Stadium, he would undoubtedly receive that exactly that at Emirates Stadium, with reports indicating that internally he is regarded as the primary target, with Arteta 'smitten' at the prospect of bringing Vinicius to the club.

There is, however, a general acknowledgement that any transfer would be far from straightforward, even with a financial willingness to push the move through should it prove feasible.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arteta has previously succeeded in persuading transfer targets that Arsenal represented their finest option, having won the race for the likes of Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber and David Raya. Given how meticulous the 44-year-old is, he will have almost certainly put together a detailed plan for how Vinicius would slot into his setup.

There is little question he would become Arsenal's standout star — a status he no longer commands at Real. Since the arrival of Kylian Mbappe, he has been overshadowed as their headline act, and a strong case could be made that Jude Bellingham also carries a bigger profile.

Since Jose Mourinho took charge, the La Liga heavyweights have been extremely active in the transfer market. Ibrahima Konate, Bernardo Silva and Denzel Dumfries have all arrived on free transfers, while Marc Cucurella has completed a £51.8m switch from Chelsea.

‌



Real are now pursuing Manchester City midfielder Rodri and have struck a substantial agreement with RB Leipzig for winger Yan Diomande.

View 2 Images Yan Diomande is set to sign for Real Madrid

Should both of those costly deals be finalised, a high-profile departure may become necessary, with Vinicius potentially the one to make way — particularly given he could walk away for nothing next summer.

‌



As for Arsenal, they are yet to splash the cash in any meaningful way, with Christos Tzolis, Illian Meslier and Piero Hincapie representing their only permanent acquisitions.

Jakub Kiwior and Leandro Trossard have already departed, while the futures of Reiss Nelson, Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Ben White and Ethan Nwaneri remain uncertain, with all potentially available for transfer.

Sports.title: Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer

Chelsea have already made big moves in the transfer market this summer and Xabi Alonso has now set his sights on Brighton's veteran striker to beef up his attack

View 2 Images Danny Welbeck is a target for Chelsea (Image: Izzy Poles/AMA)

Danny Welbeck has emerged as an unlikely transfer target for Chelsea, who are in talks to sign the veteran Brighton striker.

‌



The Blues have already been active in the transfer market this summer, making Morgan Rogers the most expensive British footballer ever in a mega-bucks £117million deal. They have also agreed a deal worth in excess of £52m for Crystal Palace's Maxence Lacroix — and their spending is not expected to stop there.

‌



Xabi Alonso is pulling the strings after agreeing to become Chelsea's new manager and it seems as though he has his sights set on an experienced Premier League striker to beef up his attack.

‌



The Mail report that Welbeck is on the Blues' radar with the 35-year-old having just 12 months left to run on his current contract with Brighton.

Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers READ MORE :

The Seagulls are aware of Chelsea's interest in Welbeck, who scored 13 times in 37 Premier League games last season.

Alonso is keen on landing the former Manchester United and Arsenal star, whose leadership qualities would be a significant boost to the Blues.

‌



Welbeck started his career at Old Trafford, coming through United's academy before moving on to Arsenal. Following a year at Watford, Welbeck joined Brighton back in October of 2020 and has enjoyed his peak years on the south coast, scoring 51 goals in 201 games.

While Welbeck is settled on the south coast, the chance to join a Chelsea side who are determined to re-establish themselves among the Premier League's elite under Alonso could give the striker a chance to challenge for silverware in the twilight years of his career.

View 2 Images Welbeck scored 13 Premier League goals for Brighton last season (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

‌



Chelsea endured a tumultous 2025-26 campaign; they parted ways with Enzo Maresca on January 1 and went on to finish 10th in the Premier League, missing out on European qualification altogether.

Alonso was lined up as Chelsea's primary managerial target after leaving Real Madrid earlier in the season. The former Liverpool midfielder started his new role earlier this month after penning a four year contract.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's gesture to Argentina squad leaked after World Cup dressing room theories
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's gesture to Argentina squad leaked after World Cup dressing room theories

Lionel Messi has seemingly put to bed any talk of trouble in the Argentina camp

View 5 Images Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain (Image: Dan Mullan)

Lionel Messi has crushed any notion of discord in the Argentina squad after he gifted his team-mates presents after their World Cup final defeat to Spain. The revelation comes courtesy of Kelci-Rose Bowers, the English partner of Argentina and Spurs defender Marcos Senesi.

‌



Bowers, 22, a footballer in her own right, took to TikTok to show off the items Messi gave to his colleagues. First, she showed off a caramel-coloured bag with her partner’s name, the Argentina badge and the World Cup logo emblazoned on it.

‌



The Inter Miami star also gave his team a golden Stanley Cup engraved with his own logo, along with a separate cup. All the items are believed to facilitate mate, a popular South American drink

‌



Bowers said she had been tasked with keeping the luxury gift "safe" by her partner, adding that it was "pretty cool that I’ve got it".

Theories over a potential issue distracting Argentina players in the World Cup final were sparked after footage emerged of Messi's strange pre-match speech. The rumours were given credence with Argentina clearly subpar in the 1-0 loss to Spain.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic quits football days later as statement released READ MORE :

Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl READ MORE :

Footage from inside the tunnel before the game showed Argentina players emerging from their dressing room. Messi was captured saying: "Come on, boys, let's forget what happened, as if nothing had happened."

Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez and Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez were two players in the background of the video, appearing visibly upset. The latter was sent off, while Martinez went off injured.

View 5 Images Kelci-Rose Bowers with the gold Stanley Cup on TikTok (Image: TikTok/@_kelci.rose)

‌



Scenes after the game, with Argentina players becoming embroiled in several brawls with their opponents, also seemed to hint at some underlying anger bubbling over.

Yet Messi's gifts seem to suggest all is well in the camp. Despite Bowers hailing from Fareham, Hampshire, and even playing for the Lionesses, the defender was spotted wearing Argentina-affiliated clothing at several matches throughout this summer's tournament as she supported Senesi.

Her pivot to supporting England’s great and historical rivals has been controversial, given her past. In 2022, Bowers played for her country at under-21 level and posted a photo of herself lining up for the English women's national side, captioning it: "Always an honour to wear this shirt."

‌



5 View 5 Images Bowers shows off the bag (Image: TikTok/@_kelci.rose) 5 View 5 Images Lionel Messi hinted at a pre-match issue for Argentina during the speech to his team-mates before the World Cup final (Image: TyC Sports)

She was present in the stands for Argentina's victory over England in the semi-finals. However, while she celebrated with her boyfriend after the final whistle, she reinforced her allegiance to England in her Instagram story, posting: "Proud of my country."

‌



She recently told The Times: "I grew up wearing an England shirt and had the privilege of representing England, so that connection will always be incredibly strong.

"[But] when your partner is playing in one of the biggest games of his career, naturally you want him to do well too. I'll be supporting Marcos personally while still feeling incredibly proud whenever I see England on a stage like this. I'm incredibly proud of him.

View 5 Images Marcos Senesi and Kelci-Rose Bowers have dated for a couple of years (Image: _kelci.rose_/Instagram)

‌



"Supporting Argentina, embracing the culture in Argentina and posting on my social media wearing the Argentina shirt is something that I've been doing. And I don't really feel like there's anything wrong with that."

After a period in the USA playing for Louisiana State University, Bowers returned to the UK, settling in Portsmouth. She then joined Bournemouth, where she met former Cherries centre-half Senesi, but has since left the South Coast-based club.

Senesi moved to Spurs on a free transfer this summer. The centre-back was a late recruit to Argentina’s World Cup squad after Leonardo Balerdi was ruled out through injury.

Sports.title: 7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season
Sports.content:
This summer is supposed to herald a new era for Manchester United after the turnaround sparked by Michael Carrick's arrival, but the momentum will only be sustained if further transfers are done.

Carrick inspired a massive improvement at United after taking over in January following the departure of Ruben Amorim. Competing in just one competition, United became consistent and finished third in the Premier League.

Now they need to build upon the platform he helped create. Further deals are needed to shape a squad depth that is capable of competing across competitions.

With pre-season in full swing, here Mirror Football asssesses United's position; the work already done, which players need to be sold and who they should sign.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Done deals

Out

Rasmus Hojlund to Napoli (£38m)

Andre Onana to Trabzonspor (loan)

‌



Casemiro (released)

Tyrell Malacia (released)

Jadon Sancho (released)

United are actually yet to negotiate a single transfer exit this summer. Hojlund's move to Napoli was an inevitability, due to a clause in his loan agreement being met, while Onana was simply loaned back to the same club he spent last season at.

‌



Casemiro, Malacia and Sancho left after their deals expired and there is still work to be done to get rid of unwanted players and their wages.

View 5 Images Youri Tielemans is a good signing - but more are needed (Image: Getty Images)

In

Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa (£35m)

‌



Andrey Santos from Chelsea (£50m)

Karl Darlow from Leeds (free)

Tynan Thompson from Tottenham (£8m)

Kit Margetson (compensation fee)

‌



United have completed two significant transfers to bolster their midfield following the departure of Casemiro. Tielemans is a ready-made Premier League performer and a true all-rounder who can be expected to slot straight into the side, while Santos has plenty of potential, but they are still some way short in terms of incomings.

Deals that need to be done

Outs

The arrival of Darlow to become Senne Lammens' back-up made it clear that Altay Bayindir no longer has a future at the club. United have already loaned out Onana once again and need to find a permanent move for Bayindir back to Turkey.

Radek Vitek started in goal for United in their 5-0 friendly win over Rosenborg, with Lammens still away on holiday after the World Cup, but is a valuable asset that needs to be cashed in on. The 22-year-old impressed on loan at Bristol City and is valued at £10m - funds that can be reinvested in more important areas.

View 5 Images Radek Vitek could bring in valuable funds (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Joshua Zirkzee has been made available for a transfer, having failed to make the grade at Old Trafford since a £36.5m move two years ago. They will have to cut their losses to offload the forward, who has a pitiful nine goals in 75 appearances for the club in total, but Juventus are reportedly interested.

The most pressing need undoubtedly lies with Marcus Rashford, who remains a United player after his move to Barcelona failed to materialise. He is a wanted man, having returned 14 goals and 14 assists for Barca last season, but his £325,000-a-week contract, which still has two years left to run, has handcuffed him to United.

A move to Fenerbahce or Galatasaray was turned down by Rashford, while United don't want to sell to a Premier League rival. He could end up staying if the deadlock continues.

View 5 Images Marcus Rashford's wages hold the key to unlocking so much for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ins

Despite signing two midfielders, Carrick wants another one. Casemiro has left and Manuel Ugarte has a serious injury, which has scuppered a summer transfer away from the club, meaning another player is needed for depth after a deal for Atalanta's Ederson fell through.

Brighton's Carlos Baleba has long been admired by United, but came off the boil last season and would still command a big fee. Bournemouth's Alex Scott is a player on the rise, but there is a premium attached to English talent, as shown by Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers' fees this summer.

Manu Kone represents a cheaper alternative. Roma are under pressure to sell the France World Cup star, who has reportedly agreed personal terms with United, due to financial issues. Roma want €60m (£51m) for the central midfielder - a fee United are unwilling to pay, so are negotiating, albeit slowly.

Carrick is also keen to sign another versatile attacker. Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha were all successes after joining last summer, but the departures of Jadon Sancho, Alejandro Garnacho and the potential exit of Rashford has left United a bit short in wide areas.

‌



View 5 Images Manu Kone could be on his way to Old Trafford this summer (Image: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Patrick Dorgu showed promise as a left winger, while Mason Mount can play out wide, yet a specialist would make sense. United bid for Crysencio Summerville before he left West Ham for Al-Hilal instead and spoke to Antoine Semenyo before he joined Manchester City in January.

United have signed Tynan Thompson, yet he is one for the future, not now. The likes of Bradley Barcola, who has been linked with a move from Paris Saint-Germain to Arsenal, and Rafael Leao are almost certainly out of reach unless Rashford is sold.

The other position Carrick has identified is left-back, where Luke Shaw is left as the only senior player, with Harry Amass as a back-up, following Malacia's departure and Dorgu's emergence as a left-sided attacker. Diego Leon hasn't made any progress since joining last summer and Fulham's Antonee Robinson and Newcastle's Lewis Hall are targets.

‌



Robinson has eye-catching pace and is an exciting attacker on the overlap, while Hall's cross ability from deep is a potential route to goal. Whether Newcastle would sell is another matter, having already lost Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, with Bruno Guimaraes also a potential departee.
