Sports.title: Jermain Defoe threatens legal action over 'untrue' Woking claims since leaving job
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe threatens legal action over 'untrue' Woking claims since leaving job

Jermain Defoe left his role as Woking manager after four months but a bitter row has broken out over his exit from the National League side

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe's representatives have hit out over a statement issued by Woking chief Jody Brown. (Image: PA)

Former England striker Jermain Defoe intends to take legal action after a statement from Woking director of football Jody Brown. The National League side parted ways with the Premier League icon less than two weeks before the beginning of the season after Defoe admitted it was 'impossible to continue'.

‌



A bitter row has broken out between the 43-year-old and Cards chief after he defended the club's transfer policy in light of Defoe's departure.

‌



Brown thanked and praised the former Tottenham Hotspur, Sunderland and Rangers striker for his work during his four months in charge. But while the Woking chief was reluctant to divulge details, he accused Defoe of not turning up to a meeting with the directors, head of operations and the management team.

‌



The 4 transfers Arsenal must complete for Mikel Arteta to win another Premier League title READ MORE :

Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

As a result of the statement, Surrey Live contacted the former striker's representatives, who replied: “The statement issued by Jody Brown is highly detrimental to Jermain’s reputation, and amounts to a serious defamation of character.

"The statement also suggests that Jermain was making unreasonable demands, which is simply untrue.

“Jermain is therefore taking immediate legal advice and intends to pursue appropriate legal action in relation to the statements made.”

‌



Defoe's departure on the eve of the new campaign sparked concerns and questions among the wider community. It prompted criticism towards the Woking hierarchy, leading Brown to launch a defence on social media platform X.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Brown said in a statement published online: “Jermain’s feedback was always positive, and he regularly expressed his enthusiasm and excitement for the season, both publicly and privately. I can therefore appreciate the surprise and subsequent speculation surrounding his sudden departure.

‌



“However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns. To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season.

"That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received. A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and Head of Operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session.

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe pictured alongside Jody Brown after being unveiled as Woking head coach. (Image: PA)

‌



"Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons. Every football club faces challenges. Players want more game time, improved contracts or transfers. The media team might want better equipment, the medical department more interns, the strength and conditioning staff larger gym space. and the car park attendants may want more coffee.

"But people do not just fail to turn up. The experience has highlighted lessons for both myself and the club, particularly around communication with Jermain and his representatives throughout the four months and six matches he was with us. Throughout that period, the club’s objective remained the same: to support the players and staff and give the project every opportunity to succeed."

Woking begin their league campaign at home to Sutton United on August 8. Craig Ross and Jake Hyde has been instructed to take charge of the Cards on an interim basis.

Article continues below

Their search for a third manager in six months is underway after Defoe replaced Neal Ardley in March on the back of six defeats in nine National League matches.

Ross and Hyde were installed on a temporary basis four months ago after Ardley's tenure came to an end on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Marine in the FA Trophy quarter-final.

Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau confronts his own behaviour as marmite LIV Golf star speaks out
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau confronts his own behaviour as marmite LIV Golf star speaks out

Bryson DeChambeau has opened up about his behaviour, which has made him a divisive star on tour

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau in action for LIV Golf (Image: Jason Butler, Getty Images)

Bryson DeChambeau has spoken candidly about his commitment to engaging with fans and signing autographs, revealing that his modest upbringing shaped his determination to make golf more accessible to people from all walks of life.

‌



The 32-year-old has built a profile that extends well beyond the fairways, cultivating a YouTube channel with more than 2.7 million subscribers and welcoming some of sport's biggest names — among them NBA icon Stephen Curry — onto his platform. Yet despite his considerable fame, DeChambeau remains one of the most approachable figures in professional golf, rarely declining an autograph and always willing to stop for a photograph.

‌



While he has had run-ins with Rory McIlroy and rubbed some up the wrong way, DeChambeau always has time for his fans. Despite his considerable fame, DeChambeau remains one of the most approachable figures in professional golf, rarely declining an autograph and always willing to stop for a photograph.

‌



Speaking to Mirror US Sport at the US Open, DeChambeau was open about the roots of that attitude. Growing up in Clovis, California, in a household where money was tight, the prospect of travelling to compete in tournaments felt out of reach.

"As time has gone on out here at LIV, you're playing around the globe quite a bit," said DeChambeau. "You're feeling and experiencing different grasses and learning how to compete under those conditions.

"I feel like, if anything, it's made me a more well-rounded golfer and given me the ability to learn in different situations because I wasn't fortunate to have that as a kid. I played in my area, and that's it. I didn't have the ability to go travel nor the money to go travel."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I mean, it's an honour. It's a crazy honour," DeChambeau added, referring to the popularity and attention he's gained throughout his career.

"I can't believe a kid from Clovis, California, that struggled to get into tournaments, because we didn't have any money growing up. Not too much. I mean, we had a mom who made a good salary, and my dad made an okay salary, but we really didn't have much."

‌



View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau says he is growing in the game (Image: Getty)

The Ryder Cup star has endured a difficult major season, yet his 2026 LIV Golf record includes two victories as the Saudi-backed tour faces a potential collapse amid funding cuts.

Despite failing to make the cut at the first three majors, DeChambeau insisted his LIV Golf campaign has been hugely impressive.

‌



"It's funny, I feel like I've had my best year out here this year, and for whatever reason, I feel like I've left a lot out there, which is quite interesting to me, but very grateful for having a great year out here," said DeChambeau.

"I don't really know what to say. I feel like this year I was ready to go. I felt ready to go this year. It didn't work out that way in the majors. I feel really comfortable with my game, as comfortable as I felt in a long time."

DeChambeau's future remains uncertain as LIV Golf continues its search for fresh investment to safeguard the tour's survival beyond 2026.

Sports.title: 'Pressure is on Antonelli' - Norris not ruling out title fightback
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has not ruled out mounting a title fightback and says all the pressure is on Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Norris claimed McLaren's first Grand Prix win of the season on Sunday with an impressive performance at the Hungarian Grand Prix and sits fifth in the Drivers' Championship, 91 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining.

Last year, Max Verstappen was 104 points off the championship lead with 10 events to go and fell just two points short of the title, which was won by Norris.

"The pressure is on him [Antonelli] for sure. There's no pressure on me. I've been feeling very confident," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

"They [Mercedes] have made more mistakes as a team and we have made less and we have come strong but I expect them to still win races and expect us to win more races. We just need to be perfect from here on now for the whole year.

"We need to improve the car still. We were certainly the quickest in Hungary from qualifying to the race. Not every race is going to be this simple, and we are going to be as quick, so we need to work hard to try to get the car to be this good to get the car to be this good everywhere. If we can, maybe that's a genuine question."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

McLaren brought a major upgrade packaged to Hungary, including a new floor, which has given them a big chunk of pace, having been able to fight at the front for most of the season.

Team principal Andrea Stella expects everyone to continue to bring new parts after the summer break, so McLaren must continue to improve too.

"Like it's always been in this 2026 season, it's a matter of a race of upgrades. The good news is that McLaren is now back in this race of upgrades, while fighting for the lead," he said.

"But I expect that the car that will be the best car at the end of the season will keep adding tenths of a second in the next 11 races, probably as much as half a second. So definitely a lot of work ahead of everyone, not only McLaren."

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

Norris defends pit priority call in Hungary

Norris lost out to Piastri on the opening lap of Sunday's race and was stuck behind his team-mate, despite clearly having more pace in hand.

He eventually used that speed advantage around the second pit stop phase by running longer than Piastri and overcutting the Australian. Prior to that moment, Norris wanted to pit first and had stated on the radio he was "miles faster".

"I just want to win the race. There are certain rules we have as a team, and we can't harm each other's race by being overly aggressive and wanting to win," said Norris in the press conference.

"But I want to win, and I certainly had much better pace than him. We had a much better chance of winning the race, let's say.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

"When I was stuck behind Oscar, Max was three or four seconds behind, and at that point he's still a threat. Ahead, there's no threat, and we have a lot more of a guarantee that we'll win as a team anyway.

"So, I wanted to box and undercut because my pace would have been so good, I could have pulled away a whole pit-stop window, I think, on him and boxed again if I needed to. Or I get him to box early. I think we were on the fine line between boxing too early and harming both of our races.

"So, it was just in the best interests of the team, which they rightly have to say back against me. But I want to do whatever I can to try and win a race, of course."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

Norris has generally had the upper hand over Piastri in recent races and many feel the British driver is performing just as well as last year when he became world champion.

The McLaren driver is unsure why his pace advantage was so significant in Hungary but hopes he continues to have the same feelings in the car after the summer break.

"The cars are identical, and I've just been feeling very strong lately. I've worked on many areas from last year," he said.

"I feel much more confident lately with how to extract performance, and I've worked a lot with my engineers to understand this car because it's certainly not an easy car to understand and figure out how to drive on the limit consistently.

"So, why? Just hard work. Hard work from my engineers and from myself to improve me as a driver and improve my driving. That is the answer."

Sports.title: What Arsenal's interest and Real's Diomande pursuit mean for Vini Jr
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior's Real Madrid future has been the subject of recent speculation, with Arsenal exploring a deal for the forward, but what could happen next?

What is the latest on Vinicius Jr?

Brazil star Vinicius Jr, 26, is entering the final year of his contract at Real Madrid.

Negotiations over an extension have dragged on without a breakthrough and it has caused increasing speculation over his future at the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Vinicius Jr's five best Real Madrid goals in LaLiga last season

That intensified last week when it emerged that Arsenal are interested in signing him this summer if he cannot agree a new deal at Real.

Meanwhile, Real Madrid have made a significant move for another winger - the exciting Ivory Coast international Yan Diomande at RB Leipzig.

It means doubts around Vinicius' future at the Bernabeu have grown over the past few days.

How serious is Arsenal's interest and can they afford him?

Arsenal's interest is real but in the early stages and conditional on a number of factors, not least the cost - which would be significant should the door open for Vinicius to leave Real.

There have been no club-to-club talks and there is no guarantee it progresses to a formal bid.

Arsenal, as newly-crowned Premier League champions, are looking to add another top-class forward despite signing Christos Tzolis. He was brought in to replace Leandro Trossard and there is doubt around the future of Gabriel Martinelli.

Last year they were keen on Vinicius's Real Madrid team-mate Rodrygo, while this summer Sky Sports News has reported their interest in Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers, who has since joined Chelsea from Aston Villa.

With one year left on his contract, the financial side of purchasing Vinicius would not be as severe as it previously has been - but it is worth remembering the sheer scale of an offer for the player two years ago from the Saudi Pro League.

Image: Vinicius Jr's stats from last season at Real Madrid

They were ready to pay him €1bn over five years and a transfer fee to Real Madrid of more than £300m (around €350m), which would have made him the most expensive transfer in history.

It would not cost anywhere near that much this time, but it gives a sense of what both Real and Vinicius were willing to forego in 2024.

Although the exact figure is confidential, Vinicius is believed to earn between €15m and €17m net per year. That's around £247,000 to £279,000 per week after tax. To earn that amount in the UK, Arsenal would need to pay him somewhere between £450,000 and £500,000 per week.

That would make him Arsenal's highest-paid player by far. Bukayo Saka is widely believed to be the current highest-paid, earning more than £300,000 per week.

A report in The Telegraph this morning claims Arsenal would be willing to go to £400,000. But that would still not equal Vinicius' current salary. Widespread reports in Spain claim that part of the current impasse with Real stems from his increased salary demands.

So is it just a dispute over a new contract?

Image: Vinicius Junior celebrates after scoring for Real Madrid in last season's Champions League clash with Manchester City at the Etihad

The situation has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest, further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms. Sky Sports News reported on Monday morning that there will be further talks this week between Real and Vinicius' representatives, with Arsenal monitoring things closely.

Image: Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr is one of the most sought-after players in world football

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.

What's the latest on Diomande?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande addressed speculation surrounding his future when he ws on World Cup duty - but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger

Real Madrid have upped their offer for winger Yan Diomande during talks with RB Leipzig, according to Sky in Germany.

They are reporting the offer, worth between £94m and £98m, has not been rejected yet, but further talks are required to satisfy Leipzig's demands.

According to Sky in Germany, around £102m is considered a realistic final price for Diomande, with Leipzig seeking a higher guaranteed fee from Real Madrid.

As things stand, there is no final agreement, but Leipzig are expecting the deal to be completed soon. Leganes have a sell-on clause for between five and eight per cent of the sale.

Diomande is at Leipzig and continues to train with the German club.

At the figures being discussed, Diomande looks set to become the most expensive African player ever, surpassing the £72m Arsenal paid for Nicolas Pepe in 2019.

Does Real Madrid's pursuit of Diomande impact Vinicius Jr?

Sky Sports News has been told Real's proposed deal for Diomande has no real bearing on the Vinicius situation. It says nothing about their desire to keep Vinicius, and only suggests they see a front three with both of these players in the team.

Diomande can play on the right wing as well, and he only strengthens the attacking options of the biggest club in the world.

According to Spanish newspaper AS, the players whose futures would be affected by Diomande's arrival are more likely to be striker Goncalo Garcia - who is wanted by Fulham - and winger Brahim Diaz. Rodrygo is still recovering from a long-term injury, so Diomande has space to come into the team quickly, even at only 19 years old.

What is the most likely outcome?

At this stage, all signs still point to Vinicius signing a new deal with Real Madrid. The fact that they will all meet again this week to discuss this suggests this is the direction of travel.

It will most likely come down to how closely Vinicius' earnings can approach those of Mbappe and satisfy his Galactico status in the squad. Normally, you do not say no to Real Madrid.

Real would not want to go into the new season with his contract running down and the resulting intensification of media speculation.

Arsenal's interest is likely to become more concrete only if the renewal fully fails, so this week is a crucial one.

Sports.title: Chelsea hold positive talks with Brighton over Welbeck
Sports.content:
Chelsea have held positive initial talks with Brighton about a deal for Danny Welbeck.

With a year remaining on his contract, Brighton do not want to stand in the striker's way as long as they get a fair price for his sale.

Welbeck has continued to be a reliable goalscorer in the Premier League at 35 years old. Last season he scored 13 times, after scoring 10 in the previous campaign.

His potential arrival would be another example of Chelsea prioritising physically imposing players with Premier League experience this summer.

They have already signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m - a record fee for a British player - and are close to bringing in Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.

It would also place further doubt on the futures of strikers Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu.

Chelsea have signed several players from Brighton in recent seasons including their main striker Joao Pedro, plus Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and Robert Sanchez.

A number of Brighton staff members have also moved to Stamford Bridge over the past four years, including sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell.

Chelsea raiding Brighton again - but this time is different

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

Chelsea moving for a Brighton player is not out of the ordinary. However, Chelsea moving for a Brighton player in their mid-30s is.

The BlueCo era has been defined by hoarding some of the best young talent on the planet and developing them in-house. That method has had some successes, but overall, it hasn't panned out.

There is clearly some recognition and accountability from the top brass about that. In bringing in Xabi Alonso as manager, they know they have lucked out in getting one of the most highly sought-after tacticians in the game. The Spaniard has clearly identified the need for experience and the club are following his lead.

The interest in Granit Xhaka earlier in the summer were among the first signs of the shift. Even making a move for Crystal Palace's Maxence Lacroix is evidence of a change in approach.

Welbeck, though, is the biggest indicator yet. Is he going to start every week? No. However, Chelsea's four senior strikers have an average age of just 23. Combined, they have made 269 Premier League appearances and scored 74 goals.

The Brighton veteran has 400 appearances and 90 goals on his own. Chelsea are crying out for these experienced heads to guide the way. Alonso has identified that and those above him seem to be finally taking notice.

Sports.title: The story of the 'non-League Wrexham' now chasing the EFL dream
Sports.content:
Having sold 40 per cent of influencer marketing agency, Goat, in 2021, Harry Hugo had made his fortune at 26 - and he realised that, by the age of 30, he would have the rare luxury of not needing to work again.

So, by his own admission, he chased moments of "instant gratification". But he also knew he needed to find a purpose.

One day, he and his friends - who had worked with him since he started his first business aged 16 - visited a Ferrari garage. He had his eyes on a 458 Spyder in black.

"My mate asked me why I was considering buying it," he tells Sky Sports.

Image: Farnham Town have earned three promotions in four seasons since Harry Hugo became chairman (Image: LJP Photos)

"My only answer was that it would be fun. That wasn't a good enough answer, so I challenged my mates to come up with something that would provide as much fun for the money.

"The first suggestion was, why don't we buy a football club - and I thought that was quite a good idea!"

The group built a matrix to rank the non-League clubs within a 50-mile radius of his home. Leatherhead came out on top, so Hugo followed the Tanners - then in the Isthmian Premier Division, one below the National League South - for six months.

Image: Hugo sold 40 per cent of influencer marketing agency Goat in 2021 and the remainder two years later (Image: LJP Photos)

When he met the board, there was scepticism, he says. "I get that as, one, it's unusual for a young guy wanting to go and spend loads of money on a football club and, two, there have been a lot of negative stories in non-League, where people have put loads of money in then walked away."

Hugo was left deflated when a deal to take over did not materialise, yet he soon realised he had not fallen in love with Leatherhead, but non-League in general and "the raw emotion, the old-school nature of football in its purest form."

Town takeover leads to back-to-back-to-back

Number two on the matrix was Farnham Town. Hugo had grown up in local area attended school in the town - which is around 11 miles from Guildford, Surrey - so there was a tie-in. The only downside? They were another two tiers down the pyramid.

But the board were instantly receptive and a deal was completed within five weeks.

Soon, the reality of what he had inherited caught up with him.

"When we walked in, it cannot be understated how s*** it was here," he says, overlooking the pitch at The Memorial Ground, which is looking in excellent condition, despite the intense recent heatwaves.

"It was the clubhouse, a stand behind the goal… and that was it. A concrete block wall around the side of the pitch and a fence across the top. I was embarrassed to bring my wife down here!"

Today, it is almost hard to believe it is the same stadium. But more on that shortly as, to understand why that is the case, one must look at Farnham's incredible rise, led on the pitch by manager Paul Johnson.

In 2022/23 - Hugo's first season - Farnham finished sixth in the Combined Counties Premier Division South.

In 2023/24, they won that same division with 108 points.

In 2024/25, they won the Isthmian South Central Division with 102 points.

Image: Paul Johnson has been in charge of Farnham Town since November 2022 (Image: LJP Photos)

And in 2025/26, they finished second to Walton & Hersham in the Southern League Premier Division South, before beating Gloucester City 5-1 in the play-off final to reach the National League South.

Before Hugo's arrival, the club had never played above the ninth tier of English football. In 2026/27, they will play in the sixth.

Do Farnham have any recognisble faces? Sam Hutchinson: Five Premier League games for Chelsea, 207 games for Sheffield Wednesday in all competitions

Brandon Mason: Two Premier League games for Watford, 36 League One games for Coventry City

Rakish Bingham: 64 Scottish Premiership games for Hamilton Academical

Billy Clifford: 31 League One games for Colchester United and Walsall, 43 League two games for Crawley Town

Aaron Kuhl: Six Championship games for Reading, five Scottish Premiership games for Dundee United

Wrexham links and the value of socials

Naturally, there have been comparisons to Wrexham, who are the most high-profile example of a club achieving back-to-back-to-back promotions, from the National League to the Sky Bet Championship.

"I'm OK with that!" says Hugo, with a laugh.

"Like them, we also care about media, brand, image, experience and the biggest thing is they brought people up; they made more National League and EFL teams look at themselves and think they could be doing it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac reflect on their five years as Wrexham owners.

"We're having the same impact on teams at step three, four, five and wondering, if they did it, why can't we?"

While the Red Dragons have their Disney+ series 'Welcome to Wrexham', Farnham produce 'Non-League Diaries', which is released weekly on YouTube.

Hugo harnessed his connections to get social media collective The Sidemen to sponsor the team in his first season, while last September, the club went viral after former Liverpool and England striker Peter Crouch walked out as a mascot as a forfeit for losing his Fantasy Football League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Due to a forfeit, Peter Crouch agreed to become Farnham Town's mascot - and drew a record attendance for the non-League side!

From 2023 until earlier this summer, Love Island runner-up Harry Cooksley was a key member of the squad and, on TikTok, they boast over 150,000 followers.

"Social media is huge commercially, from a fan engagement and brand-awareness point of view. It's weird the amount of people that know about Farnham Town," Hugo adds.

Image: Harry Cooksley (left) of Love Island fame played a key role in Farnham's rise (Image: LJP Photos)

"They might not have ever come, but they know Crouchy walked out in a full kit as a mascot or we won the play-off final 5-1 or we hold the British record for the most wins in a row in a league campaign. Other clubs have done things like it, but they can't get the message out; they can't tell the story.

"We've done a really good job of doing that and it's been a major focus because it's my background. It's the perfect distribution channel that allows us to tell that story."

Rapid rise forces need for rapid growth

Online, some accuse him of just throwing money at it. He accepts that was "a legitimate point" in his second year as getting out of the ninth tier became imperative.

"People who keep the lights on do an amazing job and make sure these non-League football clubs exist, then there's the people who are trying to push it forward. That's good for everybody," he says.

"Farnham doing things for the first time and being as successful as we have been on and off the pitch drives everybody to be better. People have gone from hating us to admiring us because they've seen someone who is genuinely invested in this and wants to do it sustainably for the long-term.

Farnham's rise on the pitch has put strain - a welcome one at that - on Hugo and those off the pitch. Each promotion has brought a nine-month deadline for the club to bring their stadium up to the requirements for that level. The official capacity is currently 2,300, but by March 31 2027, it needs to be 3,000.

But they have not focused solely on that this summer. There are impressive new stands, but the whole club has received a makeover of the highest order. The transformation is striking.

"There's so much you have to think about off the pitch if you're as successful as we've been. It's not just about throwing money at it; it's about being strategic.

"The nice thing is we're going to have brought a fanbase through that take nothing for granted because they've seen where we've come from. Hopefully everyone comes down to support the football club because we're going to need to put a lot of cash back in the coffers with the work we've done."

"Because moving the dial from an average attendance of 1,000 to 1,500 is disproportionately harder than getting someone to spend £18, not £15, inside the ground. Once you get someone in and you give them opportunities to spend, that is way easier than trying to get someone brand new in.

"That's not necessarily about putting prices up, more giving them opportunities to spend on better things.

"That metric has improved massively since we've been involved, without the ticket prices going up much at all. We are a cheap day out."

The EFL is no longer just a pipe dream

Farnham's rise has been so quick that it is hard to believe they are only two promotions from Sky Bet League Two. The ambition to get there is significant - and growing.

"The biggest thing that drives me is that Surrey doesn't have an EFL team. That's ridiculous," says Hugo. "How doesn't one of the most affluent counties, so close to London, not have one of the 92 EFL teams?!

Surrey's top non-League teams National League: Sutton United, Woking

National League South: Dorking Wanderers, Farnham Town, Walton & Hersham

"Woking and Sutton are in the league above us and when we started, Sutton were in the EFL and we were in step five. Now there's one league between us. Who's to say Farnham can't get in ahead of all the others? Three years ago, I didn't even consider that.

"We know how to get promotions. I know it takes everything, so much stuff that people don't see, but we can actually stand up and say we think we can get to the EFL and we've proven we know how to do it, though we know it's going to get harder.

"We are obviously going to try and get promoted again this season because that's in our nature, but would it be the end of the world if we didn't? Absolutely not. But we've only ever been promoted, so it's going to be a weird feeling if we get to the end of the season and we don't have a pitch invasion!

One to keep an eye on? Local lad Owen Dean came through Farnham Town's youth ranks and has since become the club's prized asset.

The 23-year-old has played 202 games for the club since the 2021/22 season, scoring 87 goals and providing 39 assists.

"Some clubs will go through a chairman's lifetime and never have one - we've had four in four years. I'm OK with our pitch not being invaded this year! It means we'd have time to figure out our facility, get it ready, so it would be National League, EFL ready."

A long journey undoubtedly lies ahead, but it would take a brave person to bet against Hugo and Farnham, who have already changed perceptions of what a modern non-League club can be.

Several years on from that day in the Ferrari garage, it is certainly fair to say Farnham's young chairman has found the purpose he was seeking.

Sports.title: Real to hold further talks over Vinicius Jr's future this week
Sports.content:
Real Madrid will hold further talks with Vincius Junior's representatives about his future this week.

Those discussions will centre on finding an agreement over a new long-term contract.

Arsenal, who are aiming to strengthen their left-wing options this summer, are interested in Vinicius and are monitoring the situation closely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Vinicius Jr's five best Real Madrid goals in LaLiga last season

Manager Jose Mourinho wants to keep the Brazil international and the club want him to sign new terms.

However, he has has entered the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Real could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at all of the reasons why Yan Diomande is high on the radar of clubs from across the world.

Sky Sports News has been told Real Madrid's proposed deal to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig has no bearing on Vinicius's situation.

Madrid are increasingly confident of completing a deal for Diomande this week after Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race on Sunday.

Real have upped their offer for winger Yan Diomande in talks with RB Leipzig, according to Sky in Germany. They are reporting the offer, worth between £94m and £98m, has not been rejected yet, but further talks are required to satisfy Leipzig's demands.

According to Sky in Germany, around £102m is considered a realistic final price for Diomande, with Leipzig seeking a higher guaranteed fee from Real Madrid. As things stand, there is no final agreement, but Leipzig are expecting the deal to be completed soon. Leganes have a sell-on clause for between five and eight per cent of the sale.

Diomande is at Leipzig and continues to train with the German club.

Sky Sports News has reported for several months that the Premier League clubs interested in Diomande are Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande says he is fully focused on the World Cup despite transfer speculation, but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger.

But he now looks destined for the Bernabeu, and Sky Sports News understands PSG are to resume their pursuit of Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche next.

Last week, Sky Sports News exclusively revealed that Liverpool had made an approach to Monaco for Akliouche, whom PSG will only bid for at the right price.

Liverpool are also interested in PSG winger Bradley Barcola, along with Arsenal, in what is an intensive and wide-ranging market for wingers this summer.

Analysis: Vinicius Jr would be jaw-dropping signing for Arsenal

Image: Brazil's Vinicius Junior celebrates after opening the scoring in Miami (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"It's well known Arsenal are aiming to strengthen their left-wing options this summer - but a deal for Brazil ace Vinicius Jr would be a jaw-dropping addition.

"Vinicius Jr has one year left on his current Real Madrid contract so this could be the window of opportunity for potential suitors to make their move, as Real try to tie the winger down to a new deal.

"Vinicius Jr's relationship with new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has been in focus.

Image: Vinicius Jr's stats from last season at Real Madrid

Sports.title: Doyle: Scandinavia can emulate Kyprios with Goodwood Cup win
Sports.content:
Our ambassador is previewing all five days of the Goodwood, beginning with an enthralling opening day on Tuesday, featuring the Goodwood Cup.

Scandinavia poised to retain cup crown

The eagerly anticipated re-match between SCANDINAVIA and Trawlerman in the Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup (3.35) on the opening day of the Qatar Goodwood Festival is one race I'm particularly excited about in what promises to be an amazing week on the Sussex Downs.

Aidan O'Brien's reigning champion got the better of a protracted duel with Godolphin's admirable veteran in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and can confirm his superiority in the Group 1 showpiece which once again looks like being a two-horse battle.

Four years younger and arguably even better this year, he can emulate Aidan's Kyprios by winning the race twice and giving the master of Ballydoyle his fourth Goodwood Cup in five years.

Roger Varian's Yorkshire Cup winner Rahiebb makes more appeal than the rest but is up against it. He simply didn't stay the marathon trip in the Gold Cup but I can't see him laying a glove on the market leaders, even though he's dropping back half a mile.

Rejuvenated Qirat may be hard to peg back

If QIRAT gets out on the lead in the HKJC World Pool Lennox Stakes (3.00) at Goodwood I really don't see any of his rivals drawing him back.

Ralph Beckett's five-year-old, who sprung that massive surprise in last year's Sussex Stakes, impressed me from the front in the Group 3 Criterion Stakes at York last time when he wore a tongue tie for the first time.

Image: Qirat stunned Goodwood with success in the Sussex Stakes last term

He could be open to more improvement in a race that might not take a lot of winning this year and gets my vote ahead of Andrew Balding's Marvelman.

He ran a smashing race in the Chipchase at Newcastle last month on his return from a lengthy break and should be sharper this time. A Group 2 winner already, he needs to take a step forward but looks a serious danger while Witness Stand, who won this race for me last year, is better than he was able to show at Chester and can hopefully make another bold bid.

Amo colt can break his maiden in vintage

I nominated PIKACHU as a horse to follow after his big run at Newmarket so I'm not forsaking him on his re-appearance in the Coral Vintage Stakes (2.25) at Goodwood.

Charlie Johnston's Amo Racing colt galloped through the line strongly in the Superlative Stakes after hitting a flat spot and can break his maiden at the fourth time of asking over this seven furlong trip.

The likely favourite Al Hudaiba is highly talented as he showed when beating Pikachu in that Group 2 but is complicated, too, and it's interesting that Charlie Appleby reaches for the blinkers in an attempt to concentrate his mind.

A more reliable proposition may be Aidan O'Brien's Haffner, a promising son of Justify who built on his Curragh debut with a maiden win at Newmarket earlier this month. This is much tougher but he represents Team Ballydoyle for a good reason.

More to come from Burke's course winner

LIBERTY LANE, a Listed winner at Goodwood, has dropped to a tempting mark which makes him a danger to all in the opening Coral Chesterfield Cup Handicap (1.50) at Goodwood.

Karl Burke's 2024 Cambridgeshire winner hasn't raced off this mark in nearly two years and is well drawn under Clifford Lee in stall four. He hinted at a return to form at Sandown last time in first-time cheekpieces, which are retained for this assignment.

My husband Tom's (Marquand) mount Yabher is also capable of a bold show after bolting up over this course and distance in May but was disappointing at York last time so has something to prove in such a competitive handicap.

Lexington can Blitz them in sprint Handicap

The Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap (4.10) at Goodwood will be fast and furious and can go to the rapid LEXINGTON BLITZ, who ran a huge race in the Epsom Dash last month.

A course and distance winner, Robert Cowell's four-year-old looks well enough treated to win this off just a 1lb higher mark but don't under-estimate Richard Spencer's pair Run Boy Run and Twilight Calls.

Richard has a knack of winning big sprint handicaps and has enlisted the services of Ryan Moore's son Toby who claims an invaluable 7lb off Run Boy Run. He's well drawn in stall 17 for a race like this while Newmarket winner Twilight Calls remains well handicapped of a mark of 90 with the in-form Saffie Osborne in the saddle.

I'll be back with my thoughts on Wednesday's action at Goodwood, featuring the Group 1 Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes and the big juvenile sprint, the Group 3 Molecomb Stakes.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Manchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offer
Sports.content:
Manchester City are hopeful that Rodri will sign a new contract, but the club are braced for a bid from Real Madrid for the midfielder as well as moves from other suitors.

Rodri’s contract expires in June next year and he has failed to sign City’s new deal, which has been on the table for a while. The club are in talks with the 30-year-old midfielder and are optimistic that these will prove successful.

Real, however, have now altered their previous stance of not being interested in Rodri after his hugely impressive displays as captain of Spain’s triumphant World Cup campaign – he won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player – and the club are understood to be preparing a bid.

Rodri’s reliability during the summer has also allayed concern regarding his physical robustness after an injury-plagued past two seasons, although he is to undergo surgery on a back injury having returned to England from north America.

In March, Rodri hinted at a desire to play for Madrid. “Having played for Atlético [in 2018-19] before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid,” he said. “There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

Madrid’s interest in signing Rodri may well initiate interest from other elite clubs. Barcelona could move for him after Frenkie de Jong’s medial collateral ligament injury ruled him out for months, while Paris Saint-Germain are known to admire him.

View image in fullscreen Rodri won the Golden Ball at the World Cup for the tournament’s best player. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

Madrid may need to generate finance in order to sign Rodri – especially if, as expected, they sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig for a fee understood to be more than €100m (£85m) – which may mean the sale of Aurélien Tchouaméni. The 26-year-old Frenchman is thought to have agreed a new contract with the club though this has not been announced. His current deal ends in summer 2028.

Manchester United retain an interest in Tchouaméni but earlier in the window were unsure if the fee Real would demand for the midfielder – around £70m – was within their budget.

Tchouaméni’s teammate Eduardo Camavinga is also on United’s radar and would cost between €50m-€60m.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Vinícius to Arsenal? Club football’s military industrial complex kicks back into gear
Sports.content:
VENI, VINÍ, VICI?

If this is an attention economy, there is no greater attention-seeker than club football. Not content with dominating the sporting agenda for 11 months of any calendar year, it has been a summer of “look at me”, largely in vain as the Geopolitics World Cup’s often grubby charms snaffled up football focus. Often faint, sometimes shrill, the keening sound of season 2026-27 approaching, of this meaning more, was never far away as clubs congratulated or commiserated their players out in North America in grasping for relevance. And with the GWC safely bagged up, the club football military industrial complex is kicking back into gear, via the usual fashion, a transfer saga, and as is customary, one that involves Real Madrid.

The central protagonist this time of a patchwork of preparing bids, coming days, exploring moves and eventual here-we-going is Vinícius Júnior. The eternal Brazilian Ballon d’Or hopeful – and refusenik – has been linked with, gasp, Arsenal. As myriad examples in recent history prove, Liverpool’s summer of 2025 as the most obvious, winning the transfer market means little in the actual, material world. Though in the summer months, there is no levy placed on the wild fantasy scenarios being played out in the minds of Gunners fans. Arsenal plus Viní equals limitless glory, orgiastic scenes of the great man thwacking corners for Gabriel and William Saliba to convert. Leandro Trossard, farewell, the new king is in town. Though what about Christos Tzolis, the Greek flier signed just last week as replacement for the departed Belgian?

Those who profess to know about this stuff – and often get things right – suggest there are legs in this. There are, though, flags on the play. Real Madrid and Florentino Pérez, recently re-elected Madrileño overlord – have form for using monied Premier League clubs as pawns. Viní has been in contract negotiations, his current deal expiring a year hence. He is reported to earn £400,000 per week, and is hardly likely to want less. Madrid do not wish him to depart for free. And this is Arsenal, whose owners have spent big in recent years, though have sometimes baulked at top dollar. Last year, they opted for Viktor Gyökeres rather than enter the Alexander Isak affair, a move that worked out well enough and Viní’s is a very different stratosphere to such dealing.

Attached to all that flimflam is Yan Diomande, the Ivorian winger, one of those players who’s become a household name despite very few of us having the time to watch RB Leipzig. Everybody wants him, it seems, but Madrid are now said to have beaten PSG to his signature, which then opens up questions of Bradley Barcola’s potential, probably very expensive, move to Liverpool. Thus, Football Daily finds itself pulled into the miasma, that aching sense of what might be, of who will go where, what it will all look like. Just when we thought we were out, they pulled us back in.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all. To those behind their pens and papers, behind ⁠their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are ​on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness” – Fifa big cheese Gianni Infantino posts an open letter on his social media disgraces, urging detractors to “take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray” after a GWC marked by controversies including US visa restrictions affecting supporters and officials from several countries, concerns involving teams from conflict-hit regions, soaring ticket prices for fans … and the suspension of an automatic one-match ban imposed on USA USA USA striker Folarin Balogun after US president Donald Trump called Infantino directly.

View image in fullscreen Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

double quotation mark The passing of Kevin Keegan brought back memories of Hull City when Paul O’Riley, a young pro, went to Firewall FC on loan for six weeks. After his loan finished he came back raving about this kid who was so dedicated. He wanted to win all the long runs, sprints and would come back in the afternoon to run up and down the terraces with weights in his hands. Being from Donny I already knew about Kevin Keegan (also a Donny lad). Vince Grimes, a fellow pro at Hull, was always banging on about Terry Heath and a young kid called Kevin Keegan. Vince kept telling the coaching staff at Hull about Keegan and that they should buy him. Their response was they’d been to watch him play several times and didn’t fancy him. Not long after all this Keegan went to Liverpool and the rest is history. Many years later when he was managing Newcastle, I wrote to him asking if he’d allow from a lad from Australia to have a spell at Newcastle. He wrote back and said he’d be welcome. Not only that, they picked the lad up from the airport, sorted out his digs, took him to Wembley on the first-team bus for the Charity Shield game and Alan Shearer gave the lad his match boots” – Micky Dale.

double quotation mark ‘People talk about it being impossible. That means nothing. I truly believe that we can do something special” – Jermain Defoe, 6 April … ‘Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC. Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position’ – Jermain Defoe, 24 July. Apparently ‘impossible’ does mean something after all” – Phil C0ckburn.

View image in fullscreen Jermain Defoe at his Woking unveiling, recently. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Micky Dale. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham Women have provided distraction from the gloom of watching men’s team | Mark Burton
Sports.content:
The exciting football played by Tottenham’s women last season provided a much-needed antidote to the dreadful men’s team, who not only flirted with relegation but took it out on a dinner date, looked deep into its eyes and started to plan a future together.

Fortunately, that relationship fizzled out and fans were able to “celebrate” at the end of the season as Premier League status was secured. Meanwhile, Spurs achieved their highest points tally in the Women’s Super League. Highlights included a 7-2 goal‑fest against Aston Villa, a mind-bending FA Cup penalty shootout win against London City Lionesses (where the first 17 penalties were successfully slotted home) and a stream of wonder goals including a 40-yard screamer from Cathinka Tandberg.

What was this crazy split-screen experience between the two Spurs teams? For weeks I did the football equivalent of putting my fingers in my ears and going ‘LA LA LA LA’, aAs the men crumbled and the prospect loomed of Lincoln visiting the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, my Spurs men’s WhatsApp group of season-ticket holders and members went into meltdown. “Spurs crisis hotline,” I’d answer, before being unable to provide answers to pressing questions: are all those passes around the penalty area really necessary? Why aren’t Spurs signing players to plug the injury gaps?

Thankfully, there was a distraction from the gloom because three years ago my wife, son and I became Tottenham Women season-ticket holders. This move was inspired by England’s Lionesses reaching the World Cup final in 2023. We were visiting family in Australia and when England beat Colombia 2-1 in the quarter-finals, several Colombia fans made detours to shake our hands in the Brisbane fan zone. There were about 2,000 of them and approximately 20 England fans. This, I thought, is the sort of football experience I want my son to enjoy.

That positive vibe has continued as we’ve followed Tottenham. So, what explains their recent improvements? The first factor was Martin Ho’s appointment last year as the head coach. Before joining he had been an assistant at Manchester United and the head coach of the Norwegian side Brann. Behind‑the‑scenes chatter suggests players like and respect him.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ho’s arrival as Tottenham head coach ahead of last season transformed the team’s fortunes. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

He has connected with supporters by wandering occasionally through the “Legends Lounge” at Leyton Orient (where Spurs play most of their women’s home games) for pre-match chats.

The most important part, though, is that Ho has Spurs playing attacking and organised football. The players look certain of their roles and clear on how they can support each other.

Another factor has been the players who joined. The midfielder Olivia Holdt was Spurs’ top scorer last season and Toko Koga has been a stalwart in central defence. Then in January Signe Gaupset, who loves to charge through the midfield with the ball, was signed.

The way Ho worked with the existing players has also been key. In 2024-25 the team significantly underperformed, finishing one place above relegation, which led to the departure of the head coach Robert Vilahamn. Last season Spurs won five of their first six games. It is unknown what Ho said to encourage established players back to their best, but it was likely not an Igor Tudor-like speech where he told them they couldn’t attack, couldn’t defend and couldn’t run.

View image in fullscreen Cathinka Tandberg (right) scored one of the goals of last season against Everton. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

Tottenham were good at attacking, defending and running all season, and it was a pleasure to watch Eveliina Summanen, Amanda Nildén, Lize Kop, Drew Spence and Clare Hunt.

There were a couple of games where they were thumped by Manchester City, but City have Khadija “Bunny” Shaw, who has a better goals-per-game ratio than Erling Haaland. They also won the league ahead of Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United. These four clubs dominate the WSL and Spurs finished fifth behind these heavyweights. Breaking into the top four seems a real possibility in the next year or two.

Within days of last season ending, Spurs signed the highly rated Netherlands international Caitlin Dijkstra from Wolfsburg to bolster the defence and Germany’s Shekiera Martinez, who impressed as a clinical striker at a mediocre West Ham. Other proven players have followed, including Kirsty Hanson from Aston Villa and Alice Sombath from OL Lyonnes.

It has been sad to say goodbye to Bethany England and Ashleigh Neville. Neville’s desire to move closer to home by transferring to Leicester was understandable but it is perplexing that England, Spurs’ record goalscorer, was not given at least a one-year extension.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The side at the start of the season will look very different from the one we began supporting three years ago but what remains constant is the friendship and passion of our fellow season‑ticket holders.

View image in fullscreen Bethany England’s departure from Tottenham at the end of last season was an emotional affair. Photograph: Javier García/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

Their knowledge of football is extraordinarily deep. Many have been Spurs men and women fans for years, writing blogs, recording podcasts and punishing themselves by going to West Ham to stand in the rain and wind. These fans have loved Spurs women from the days when a smattering of them watched Broxbourne Ladies, as the club were then, working their way up the leagues.

Another bonus of watching the women’s game is the atmosphere. Fans will vent their frustration and respectfully inquire whether the referee has recently attended a well-known high street optician, but the swearing and anger often exhibited at the men’s games is largely absent.

Before each game fans decorate the stands with banners of Spurs players adorned with the Progress Pride flag. This visualisation of LGBTQIA+ identity shows that everyone is welcome. I hadn’t paid much attention to this until starting to support Spurs Women and it has made me much more aware of football’s potential as a positive agent for change.

Women’s football may be fractionally slower than the men’s but the games are fast-moving and there is no video assistant referee. This results in the occasional howler but it is preferable to waiting in the stands for five minutes wondering what is going on.

This season, hopefully there will be even more people going to matches and enjoying the experience of supporting the women’s game. It is difficult to recommend going to Spurs more highly, but other women’s football teams are available.

Mark Burton is a Tottenham Women season-ticket holder.

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World Cup
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives while defending the tournament ⁠as a success that celebrated ⁠unity, safety and inclusion.

In ​an open letter published on Monday, Infantino said detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of fans around the world who witnessed the tournament, ⁠won by Spain and staged in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

“You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all,” said the 56-year-old. “To those behind their pens and papers, behind ⁠their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are ​on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness.”

Fifa faced criticism about a number of issues ‌during the World Cup, including US visa restrictions affecting supporters and officials from several countries and concerns for teams from conflict-hit regions. Infantino’s letter followed scrutiny of Fifa’s suspension of an automatic one-match ban imposed on the US striker Folarin Balogun after the intervention of Donald Trump. Officiating decisions in Argentina’s last-16 victory over Egypt also received criticism, most strongly from the Egypt manager, Hossam Hassan.

“Potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent ​decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide,” Infantino said in his letter. “It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.“

The Somali referee, Omar Artan, was barred from entering the US despite having a valid visa while the Iran team and staff were subject to difficult travel restrictions imposed on them by the US government as a consequence of the war between the two countries.

“Iran ​entered the United States without ‌incident or conflict. The ​Iranian team received visas ​to enter because football is about peace. It’s not about politics,” said Infantino. “Countries facing serious health issues or other challenges were granted visas.”

Infantino’s letter is likely to lead to further criticism and ridicule of the man who on the eve of the previous World Cup in Qatar declared: “Today I feel Qatari. Today I feel Arabic. Today I feel African. Today I feel gay. Today I feel disabled. Today I feel a migrant worker.”

Sports.title: Andrea Pirlo out of running for Italy job but defends deal with Russian betting firm
Sports.content:
Andrea Pirlo has confirmed he is no longer in line to coach Italy, with his sponsorship deal with a Russian betting firm believed to behind the development. Several Italian politicians have raised concerns about Pirlo’s role as an ambassador for Fonbet, saying the national team coach should not have conflicting views on Italy’s support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

Writing on Instagram on Monday, Pirlo said he “heard last night that I’m no longer the candidate for the Italy national team job”. The former Azzurri midfielder had previously insisted the Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is “exclusively for commercial and sports purposes”, adding: “Attributing a political significance to that collaboration means attributing beliefs to me that I have never expressed and don’t belong to me.”

Pirlo added: “Over the past few days, I have watched with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of head coach of the Italian national team. Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always carried out my work in full compliance with the laws of the countries where I have worked and with the contracts I have ‌signed.“

Despite Pirlo having the backing of the new Italian football federation technical director, ‌Paolo Maldini, the controversy has created significant friction among politicians. “After yet another defeat and another missed World Cup qualification, Italian football desperately needed a cultural, ethical and managerial revolution. The choice of Andrea Pirlo goes in the exact opposite direction,” said Pina Picierno, a vice-president of the European parliament, on social media.

Ignazio La Russa, the head of the Senate and a member of the prime minister Giorgia Meloni’s party, expressed doubts over Pirlo’s possible appointment. On Saturday, La Russa said: “Of course ​I am an Italy fan ​and Pirlo was a great champion, but as a coach, it is a leap in the dark.”

Carlo Calenda, the leader of the Azione party, was even more direct in his criticism. “Anyone who is or has been promoting Russia after 2022 should not hold national office,” he said.

The FIGC turned to Pirlo – who had been prepared to leave his job as coach of Dubai United – after failing to land Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti in their search for a successor to Gennaro Gattuso, who left his post by mutual consent in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Arsenal and Liverpool battle it out for Bradley Barcola?
Sports.content:
Like baggy trousers, small sunglasses and leopard print, transfer rumours are back in a big way. And there can be no doubting the transfer ambition of the Premier League champions, Arsenal, who are eyeing up either Vinícius Júnior or Bradley Barcola as a deluxe Leandro Trossard replacement.

One sticking point for the Gunners is the former’s apparent desire to stay put at Real Madrid, while Liverpool appear to be favourites for Barcola if they can muster the £145m Paris Saint-Germain are demanding for their fourth-best forward. The path may become clear for Vinícius to leave the Bernabéu, however, with the club closing in on a deal for the Ivorian World Cup sensation Yan Diomande. Perennial prospect Endrick has also been touted for a move away from Madrid this summer.

Staying with wingers, Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye is coveted by the Saudi Pro League’s Al-Hilal, while a potential fight for the signature of Pedro Neto could be upon us, with a few Saudi clubs in the mix with Liverpool and Manchester City. Why on earth Chelsea would want to sell such a talent is a good question, but balancing the books at Stamford Bridge is imperative after the £117m splurge on Morgan Rogers. Forgotten City wide man Savinho could be heading to Tottenham to make room for any new arrival at the Etihad.

Manchester United are staying out of the scramble for wide guys and instead concentrating their efforts on centre-forwards. If Joshua Zirzkee leaves this summer – with Juventus targeting the Dutchman – Ollie Watkins, 31 before the year is out, a possible replacement. United could ship out their young left-back Harry Amass to Coventry, either permanently or on loan, which has got some fans very excited about the possible arrival of Lewis Hall.

João Palhinha’s future has been the subject of some speculation. Bayern Munich’s sporting director, Christoph Freund, has made no bones about trimming their squad, paving the way for the Portuguese to join Aston Villa, but the midfielder would prefer to stay put. Mind you, he previously said he wanted to extend his loan stay at Spurs. Marco Silva – a former manager of the midfielder at Fulham – wants him at Benfica on loan.

Remember Mohamed Salah? Well the Egyptian King is still without a club after leaving Liverpool and enjoying some holiday after the World Cup. His next stop could well be Besiktas, with a stunning Darwin Núñez reunion on the cards if the Uruguayan also joins the Turkish club from Al-Hilal. Plenty of Saudi clubs are still on the Salah case and even Sporting Kansas from MLS have been linked.

Sports.title: Real Madrid ready to seal deal for Yan Diomande after PSG pull out of move
Sports.content:
Real Madrid look to have won the race for RB Leipzig’s coveted winger, Yan Diomande, after Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the bidding war.

The Ivory Coast international has been the subject of an intense transfer saga this summer, following a breakout season in the Bundesliga and an impressive World Cup campaign.

The 19-year-old was linked with a move with Liverpool early in the window, before the player’s camp revealed he would instead prioritise a switch to Paris. However, with Real now moving ahead of PSG, Diomande looks set for the Bernabéu with the reported fee “well in excess” of €100m (£85m).

The breakthrough comes just days after Leipzig rejected Madrid’s opening proposal of €90m plus €10m in add-ons. Diomande, who has reportedly already agreed personal terms with Real, is now expected to fly to the Spanish capital for a medical.

The deal will come as a blow for PSG, who looked to be the frontrunners, with many reports suggesting they were his first choice if he did leave Germany. However, the European champions were unable to agree a fee and issued a statement on Sunday insisting they will not break their “principles”.

The statement read: “Paris Saint-Germain has this evening formally withdrawn its interest in and bids for Yan Diomande. PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance.”

Meanwhile, Liverpool have turned their attention to PSG’s Bradley Barcola as they continue to search for wingers.

Sports.title: Chiesa wants ‘new chapter’ with Iraola after frustrating time under Slot at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa has said he wants “a new chapter” at Liverpool with Andoni Iraola following a frustrating time under Arne Slot and claimed the club were lucky to qualify for the Champions League last season.

The Liverpool forward has been linked with a return to Italy this summer having struggled for minutes during his two years at Anfield. Chiesa made 36 appearances for Slot last season, a healthy return on paper, but only five were starts.

He started one Premier League game last season despite the problems Liverpool had in attack because of injuries to Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké, and his last start came in the FA Cup fourth-round win against Brighton on 14 February. A change of head coach, Chiesa hopes, will herald a change in fortune as a Liverpool player.

“It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year,” said the 28-year-old, who produced a fine finish in Liverpool’s 4-2 friendly defeat of Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. “Maybe there have been too many fresh starts [for him]. But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager.

“Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best. Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer had his gameplans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.”

Chiesa admits he has not discussed his future with Iraola since the Basque coach succeeded Slot in June. “The only conversations I had were about pressing and tactics,” he said. “He put me striker against Sunderland and he wants me there.”

But the Italy international, who has two years remaining on his Liverpool contract, claimed his priority is to prove himself to the head coach rather than seek a return to Serie A. Como and former club Juventus have been linked with a move for the forward.

“Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool,” said Chiesa. “I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.”

View image in fullscreen Federico Chiesa scored for Liverpool against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Liverpool secured Champions League qualification on the final day of a troubled season in May in what proved to be Slot’s final game in charge. Chiesa insists that was no cause for celebration at a club of Liverpool’s stature and there must be improvement next term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward said: “Liverpool deserves more. Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky.

“It was a tough season last year and this season we need to do better, in the Champions League as well. We went out to PSG. We want to go further in that competition and then we want to do even better in the Premier League as well.”

Chiesa also hopes to reclaim his place in the national team next season, having missed out on several squads recently. Italy are now searching for a new head coach, having failed to qualify for the World Cup under Gennaro Gattuso.

Chiesa said: “The situation is that I spoke to the manager a few times, Gattuso, and I was not ready physically at the time. When I got back in March, unfortunately I got injured. But I am looking forward to playing for the national team. I have won with the national team [the European Championship]. It is always nice to play and win for your national team.”

Sports.title: Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France
Sports.content:
A female referee reportedly suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee in a men's friendly match in France.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay had taken charge of the friendly between Ligue 2 French side Metz and their Dutch opponents Fortuna Sittard on Sunday.

Demoncay had blown for a free kick to Fortuna Sittard in the 39th minute, after a Metz player had pulled the shirt of a breaking attacker.

The fouled Fortuna Sittard player was then seen squaring up to two Metz players following the incident.

This led to Demoncay racing over in an attempt to break up the incident, while players from both teams also ran in as the melee grew.

Footage showed Demoncay, 26, being knocked over backwards as more players pushed into the melee.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee between players during a friendly in France

Demoncay had attempted to intervene in the brawl but was knocked down as more players got involved

One player was seen signalling for medical attention with Demoncay appearing to have hit her head on the ground after falling

While unclear on the footage, Demoncay appeared to hit her head on the ground after falling.

One Fortuna player was quick to notice the stricken referee, as they stood by the official and motioned for medical staff to come to her aid.

Medical staff, assistant referees and security came onto the pitch, with Demoncay receiving assistance.

The footage showed Demoncay sitting up as medical staff began to assess her, while players appeared to have become concerned by the incident.

Demoncay was ultimately unable to continue the match, with one of her assistants forced to step in.

The incident, which played out with a sign in the background reading 'respect the referee', led to two players being booked.

Fortuna Sittard had described it as a 'remarkable moment' on the club's website.

Metz, who had been leading 1-0 at the time, went on to win 3-1 in the friendly.
