Sports.title: Do YOU think you could beat Luke Littler at darts? The world No 1 is inviting amateurs to take him on in new Netflix show... for a prize of £501,000!
Sports.content:
Luke Littler is inviting fans to try and beat him in a leg of darts for a gobsmacking prize of £501,000.

The Professional Darts Corporation (PDC) world No 1 will star in a one-off live Netflix show on October 30, taking on 20 punters from across the nation.

Regional qualifying heats in London and Manchester are already open for sign-ups.

'Everyone thinks they can beat me,' said Littler, perhaps overestimating the public's self-confidence a tad.

'Now they get a chance to prove it. Bring it on.'

The lucky darts players who get a chance will be hoping to catch the 19-year-old on a bad day, but the prospect of that is vanishingly thin.

Luke Littler is inviting fans to play him at darts for a £501,000 prize live on a Nteflix show

The 19-year-old is aiming to complete a clean sweep of the eight PDC ranking events - but YOU could be a thorn in his side

Littler defended his World Matchplay title in scintillating style last week, averaging a record of 111.04 across the tournament. The previous record was set by Phil Taylor with 106.31 in 2010.

In the final against Gerwyn Price in Blackpool, Littler stepped up his game, averaging a devastating and record-breaking 111.53, winning 18-9.

The Nuke is aiming to complete the clean sweep of the eight PDC ranking events this year, something which has never been done before.

He is on course for that so far after winning the World Championship, World Masters, UK Open, and World Matchplay.

But he will need to take part in some Pro Tour events in order to qualify for the Players Championship Finals in November. Unfortunately, that means a family holiday in Spain will have to be sacrificed; Littler is needed in Leicester.

Littler boosted his bank balance by £225,000 after beating Price, taking his total winnings in the PDC's two-year Order of Merit to £3,143,500.

'It's been a crazy week, one of the best weeks of my life with the darts I've played,' Littler told Sky Sports after his World Matchplay triumph.

Littler was emotional after winning the Premier League against Luke Humphries in May

'It's been tough. The stats may look like it's easy, but when you're on this stage with how hot it is, it's not easy.

'I've definitely played some of the best darts of my life. I feel like it's the best version of myself. I have just played so well.'

Defeated finalist Price, the world No7, said: 'Luke is one in a million. I think I played pretty decent.

'In that game I missed a couple of opportunities but the bull checkouts, the 167, it was a big turning point even though it was early in the game.

'I didn't play brilliant, but I played decent.'

Littler has faced boos during some events and admitted that he almost walked away in the final of the Premier League Darts against Luke Humphries as a result.

‘After Brighton, I came off stage, and then in Manchester I was sat at home saying to Faith [Millar, girlfriend], “I don’t want to do it any more”. Just the crowd every week.

‘I said to her, “I’m down bad”.’

The teenager then had to stop speaking as he welled up with emotion, before Humphries added: ‘It shows what it means to us as players. Being on the road for 16 or 17 weeks - it’s hard work.’

Sports.title: Andrea Pirlo BLOCKED from becoming Italy manager after links to Russian betting firm spark 'political' concerns - as icon breaks silence on decision that has left Paolo Maldini furious
Sports.content:
Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after 'political' concerns were raised over the football legend's sponsorship deal with a Russian betting company.

Pirlo, 47, was backed by former team-mate and new Italian Football Federation (FIGC) technical director Paolo Maldini to land the role after legendary ex-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola reportedly declined the opportunity.

The former AC Milan and Juventus star was on the brink of agreeing a deal with the crisis-hit football nation before several Italian politicians raised concerns about Pirlo's role as an ambassador for Russian betting firm Fonbet.

It was felt Pirlo, who had been prepared to leave his current job as coach of Dubai United, should not have conflicting views on Italy's support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

Pirlo himself confirmed that he was no longer in the running in an Instagram post on Monday, urging that his Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is 'exclusively for commercial and sports' purposes.

His claim has been refuted by Dubai United owner Sergey Lomakin, who stated that Pirlo's involvement with the firm was not an involuntary aspect of his deal.

Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after a dramatic twist

The Italy legend's appointment has been blocked after 'political' concerns were raised over his sponsorship deal with Russian betting company Fonbet in the United Arab Emirates

Pirlo said in a statement: 'In recent days, I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of Head Coach of the Italian national team.

'Out of respect for the institutions, the Federation, and all those involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now.'

'However, I feel it is my duty to clarify certain aspects.

'Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always conducted my activities in full compliance with the laws of the countries in which I have worked and the contracts I have signed.

'The professional collaboration at the centre of the recent controversy arose as part of my career in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature.'

It is understood Maldini is furious by the decision made by FIGC president Giovanni Malago and may quit his role as technical director after Pirlo's appointment was blocked.

Adverts, endorsements and sponsorship deals pertaining to betting are strictly prohibited in Italy.

Pirlo added: 'Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing to me beliefs I have never expressed and that are not mine.

'I would like to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the esteem and trust they have shown me. I know their expertise, their seriousness, and the love they have always dedicated to Italian football.

Paolo Maldini is reportedly furious at the decision and may walk from his role as a result

'I regret that a sporting decision was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing to me meanings and intentions that are not mine.

'My love for Italy does not depend on a position. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.'

Pirlo was at best a third-choice after Carlo Ancelotti and Guardiola turned down offers to coach a team that has failed to qualify for three consecutive World Cups.

Now former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are back being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino goes full Trump as he furiously slams World Cup critics for 'spreading hate' in blistering social media rant
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino has launched a blistering attack on World Cup critics, claiming they've been 'consumed by hate' and telling them to 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' in order to 'find peace.'

With the six-week tournament officially over, Infantino took the time to address his detractors through a 15-slide post on Instagram – where he seemingly defended a number of controversies that occurred throughout the summer competition.

The outburst was posted across Infantino's personal Instagram account and cross-posted to FIFA's official page on Sunday night, reaching over 13 million followers.

Infantino, who didn't hold a press conference when the World Cup began, nor when it ended, began his outburst by calling out those 'who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception and the joy.'

He claimed that those who 'missed' out were 'so consumed by hate and criticism.'

The FIFA chief appeared to take aim at journalists as he claimed critics sat 'behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumors'.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino launched a blistering attack on World Cup critics on Sunday

In a 15-slide Instagram post, Infantino called out those who were 'so consumed by hate and criticism' that they 'missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the laughter and the joy'

'I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organizing, working hard and delivering the best show in the world,' he continued.

Infantino, 56, then claimed: 'We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 percent safety and security, only joy and happiness!'

However, critics online were quick to point out a number of violent incidents that occurred as a direct result of the six-week summer tournament.

In fact, the opening day of the 2026 FIFA World Cup was hit by violent protests as riot police fired tear gas at demonstrators prior to Mexico's game against South Africa.

The massive demonstrations were fueled by a coalition of multiple unions and activist groups marching to draw global eyes to the country's severe domestic issues.

The most prominent groups mobilizing include searching mothers' collectives, the CNTE teachers' union, federal judiciary workers and various transport organizations. In total, it was reported that eight simultaneous protests took place.

Away from the tournament's opening day, there were a number of violent incidents that occurred at fan parks and during post-match celebrations worldwide.

Most tragically, Infantino's claim of 'zero incidents' ignored the death of four supporters in Mexico City, who suffocated during chaotic street celebrations following Mexico's round of 32 victory over Ecuador.

Infantino claimed: 'We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 percent safety and security'

However, there were a number of violent incidents throughout the tournament - such as when protestors clashed with riot police prior to the very first game of the 2026 World Cup

While Mexico secured a 2-0 victory over South Africa, thousands of protesters hit the capital

While Infantino previously offered condolences on social media, the day after the tragedy, his 15-slide post made no mention of the victims when boasting about tournament safety.

Meanwhile, other fans noted that FIFA opted to proceed with the tournament despite fans from four competing nations, Iran, Haiti, Senegal and Ivory Coast, facing US travel bans imposed by the Trump administration.

In another case, Somali referee Omar Artan saw his dreams of officiating in a World Cup crushed after being prohibited from entering the US on the tournament's eve.

Trump's administration then made a bombshell claim that Artan, who was named as Africa's best male referee last year, was denied entry due to terrorism fears.

Infantino appeared to address the controversy surrounding both the fans and the official.

He wrote: 'You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world. Because football unites the world, and it was demonstrated impressively this summer.'

Elsewhere in his social media rant, Infantino claimed that 'Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.'

However, fans noted that only four of the fifteen Iranian team staff members who were originally denied visas were later granted the right to travel into the country.

Despite a number of incidents regarding visas being denied, Infantino downplayed that aspect

Somali referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan was denied entry to the United States to officiate

The Iranian Football Federation alleged that the US and FIFA did not want them at the World Cup

US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also sparked fury after claiming that 'almost half' of Iran’s non-playing delegation had direct ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

'Iranians are used to the mistreatment and lies of US officials, so no one in Iran is surprised by these hostile remarks,' an official for the federation said, via The Telegraph.

'These remarks once again demonstrate that US officials have no commitment to international law or the principles expected of a host nation capable of organizing a global sporting event.'

Infantino also appeared to fire a direct shot at critics regarding the mid-tournament storm surrounding Donald Trump and USMNT forward Folarin Balogun.

The striker was sent off during the USA's 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, meaning that he should have been unavailable for their next game against Belgium.

However, on the eve of the game, FIFA announced that they had postponed his suspension – sparking widespread fury from fans across the globe.

It was later revealed that Trump had phoned up Infantino, who previously presented the US president with an inaugural FIFA Peace Prize, and asked for the case to be reviewed, leading fans to launch accusations of political interference.

Addressing the controversy, Infantino wrote: 'Indeed, 'arguable' referees' decisions or 'strange' disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide.

Hinting at the drama surrounding Folarin Balogun's postponed suspension, Infantino claimed that instances like that 'are routine and widely accepted in the biggest leagues worldwide'

The forward, who was sent off for this tackle, will now be available to face Belgium on Monday

It later emerged that Trump had called Infantino over the matter prior to a decision being made

'It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticizing,' the FIFA chief added on the matter.

The unprecedented ruling sparked furious accusations of political favoritism from UEFA, the Belgian Football Association and countless European lawmakers.

The Norwegian Football Federation have also since confirmed plans to file a formal complaint over Trump's role in the decision.

He capped off his tirade by telling his detractors to step away from their computers and find peace.

'To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions,' Infantino concluded.

'To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn't. May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup. May football rise above all hate.'

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe admits he will be in 'pain for a while' as he releases emotional 520-word statement after France's World Cup heartbreak
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe admits he will be in 'pain for a while' as he releases emotional 520-word statement after France's World Cup heartbreak

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kylian Mbappe admits he will be hurting for a while after France's World Cup campaign ended with heartbreak.

He has posted a lengthy statement saying France fans probably deserved a 'better ending' than the 2-0 defeat by Spain in the semi-finals and the 6-4 lashing by England in the third-place game.

Mbappe, 27, won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and is now the most prolific man in World Cup history with 22.

The Real Madrid star captained his country through the final tournament of manager Didier Deschamps, who has stepped down after 14 years in charge.

Mbappe is currently on holiday but in the coming weeks he will link up with new manager Jose Mourinho as Madrid aim to take back the LaLiga title, which they haven't won since 2024.

Penning the 520-word message, Mbappe insisted that gratitude and pride were major emotions for him. He wrote: 'Thank you.

Kylian Mbappe says he will be hurting for a while after France's World Cup collapse

France finished fourth in Didier Deschamps' final tournament in charge - but Mbappe was the World Cup's top scorer

A month of emotion. Of pushing beyond our limits. Of pride in wearing the colors of France. And above all, of passion: the same passion that drives us on the pitch and that drives you, whether you were watching from home or cheering in the stands. That's what we experienced together. An incredible story.

'We're not bringing a collective trophy home. It hurts, and it will hurt for a while. I won't pretend otherwise. I'm proud to have won the Golden Boot, but it would have meant far more with the World Cup beside it. Maybe we owed you a better ending. But we don't always get to choose how the story ends. We do get to choose what we put into it, and we gave it everything. That much we can be proud of.

'Thank you to my teammates. Without their work, their runs, their passes, without the spirit that carried us from the first match to the last, I could never have scored so many goals. This award belongs to the team as much as it belongs to me. As a kid, I dreamed of playing in a World Cup. Just one. I've now played in three, won one, and this year I've had the immense honor of captaining my country. I will never forget it.

'So many of you stayed up late, some of you deep into the night, to watch us play an ocean away. You gathered at home, in bars, with family and friends, in France and far beyond it. Others were there with us in the stadiums, draped in the French flag. Children with stars in their eyes. Men and women of every background and every generation, united by the simple joy of sharing the moment.

'You never stopped believing in us. Not in the hardest moments. Not even when we deserved it least. This story was written by millions of hands, not just by the eleven on the field, all of them carried by the same passion.

'And I've already said to Didier what I needed to say. He knows. Thank you to him, to his entire staff, to the physios, the chefs, the fitness coaches, the drivers, and to everyone working behind the scenes whom no one ever sees and without whom none of this would have been possible. And thank you to everyone who welcomed us and supported us across the United States.

'At its heart, football is still a game. A game we take very seriously, one we spend a lifetime trying to master, but a game all the same, and it still comes down to what it came down to when we first started playing: a ball, a goal, and the desire to score. That's why it brings us together the way it does.

'This World Cup has come to an end, but the story goes on. There will be other matches, other nights in summer and in winter when we'll all come together again over this same game, with the same undiminished excitement. Our journey together is far from over.

Kylian Mbappe and his girlfriend, Ester Exposito, were spotted at a Miami nightclub in the hours after France lost to England in the third-place game of the 2026 FIFA World Cup

The image was taken hours before Mbappe posted this image of Exposito to his Instagram story before it was quickly deleted, seemingly confirming the rumours of their relationship

Ahead of the World Cup, Exposito posed in the West Village on a vacation to New York City

'Thank you for everything. Kylian Mbappe.'

As part of the post, he shared a photo of himself as a child in front of posters of Zinedine Zidane, Ronaldinho, and Thierry Henry.

Mbappe has, at least, been able to enjoy his time off after the World Cup.

Just hours after France's loss to England, Mbappe was out on the town in Miami at the LIV Nightclub inside the city's famous Fontainebleau hotel.

He was joined by his girlfriend, Spanish actress Ester Exposito, and a group of friends at a private table.

The pair had enjoyed a dinner at Papi Steak shortly before, and while at the club they enjoyed Cloonee's set from a private table, opting to stay out of the limelight.

Photos of the couple surfaced after Mbappe quickly deleted an Instagram story showing Exposito in a hotel room as she wore his full kit.

Exposito posed wearing the jersey and shorts of the French goalscorer – as well as the captain's armband.

The photo was very quickly deleted, but not before it had made its way to his story and circulated around the internet.

They have also been seen aboard a boat together.

They were also seen enjoying a meal after Exposito's native Spain won their second World Cup title by defeating Argentina 1-0.

At the time, there was no public confirmation that the two were dating. However, rumors had persisted since the spring when Exposito attended one of Mbappe's matches at Real Madrid in March.

The two were later spotted on a bowling date in Paris in April and on a yacht outing in Italy in May.

Exposito previously admitted to having mixed emotions when Spain and France met in the semifinals, telling a reporter: 'That's a difficult choice for me'.

Sports.title: Race cancelled just 24 hours after F1 confirm addition to calendar as statement released
Sports.content:
Race cancelled just 24 hours after F1 confirm addition to calendar as statement released

Formula One confirmed before the Hungarian Grand Prix that Malaysia will host the Bahrain Grand Prix, which was cancelled earlier this year due to the Iran war

View 2 Images The Sepang International Circuit will no longer host a Thailand Super Series race to accommodate the Bahrain Grand Prix (Image: Icon Sportswire, Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Formula One moving the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia means that round four of the Thailand Super Series will no longer take place at the Sepang International Circuit. The track was due to host two of the five races on its calendar, but will now host only the first this summer.

‌



A second in September was due to take place a fortnight before the rescheduled F1 race weekend. However, that is no longer possible due to their Grand Prix preparations.

‌



Surface cleaning will instead take place at Sepang. It is also said that strict safety and system checks will happen.

‌



F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges READ MORE :

The Bahrain race was scheduled for April. However, it was scrapped, alongside the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, owing to conflict in the Middle East.

Continued hostilities in the region have derailed plans to stage a race at the Bahrain International Circuit in October. That has prompted the Gulf nation to pay for a race to be held 3,750 miles away in Malaysia.

It will run from October 2 to 4, slotted between races in Azerbaijan the preceding weekend and Singapore a week afterwards. Sepang last staged an F1 race in 2017, and work is needed to prepare it for a first in almost a decade.

‌



View 2 Images Malaysia will host this year's Bahrain Grand Prix (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

A letter, addressed to "competitors and partners" of the Thailand Super Series and signed by vice president Preeda Tantemsapya, stated: "The official announcement made by Formula 1 and the FIA yesterday, that Malaysia will host the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit on October 2-4 ... means the circuit will have to be closed for strict safety, surface cleaning and system checks in preparation for the Formula 1 event.

"Hence, we regret to inform you that we have received notification from the circuit management that they are unable to proceed with the Sepang event originally scheduled for September 18-20. Following receipt of this notification, we are actively working with different parties, looking at all the possible alternative dates and plan to reschedule the event."

‌



A similar message shared on the racing series' Facebook page stated: "We sincerely apologise for this unforeseen situation beyond our control and appreciate your patience, understanding, and continued support. Further updates will be announced as soon as they become available. Thank you for your continued trust and cooperation."

Sky broadcasts every practice, qualifier and race throughout the season, as well as exclusive coverage of the Premier League, EFL, darts and golf.

F1 bosses are hopeful that the newly-confirmed Sepang race will mark the final alteration needed to the 2026 calendar. Yet uncertainty remains surrounding the final two rounds of the season in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, given that ceasefires have repeatedly collapsed in recent weeks.

F1 and the FIA will be unable to stage races in those nations if the threat of attack from either Iran or its regional allies persists. A decision doesn't need to be taken immediately, though time will become increasingly pressing come September when teams must begin dispatching freight to the Gulf.

Sports.title: Luke Littler's pursuit of the PDC clean sweep has become one of the sport stories of 2026
Sports.content:
Luke Littler's pursuit of the PDC clean sweep has become one of the sport stories of 2026

The 19-year-old kept his World Matchplay crown in spectacular fashion with an emphatic victory over Gerwyn Price and has now won all four of darts' ranking events in 2026

View 3 Images Luke Littler is targeting total domination of the darts calendar in 2026 (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

If you fancy your chances of beating Luke Littler in a game of darts, you can sign up to try and have a crack at a special Netflix show.

‌



You could win £501,000. Then again, you could not. After all, Gerwyn Price averaged 105 per visit during his World Matchplay contest with Littler and was thrashed 18-9.

‌



Littler’s domination of darts is becoming one of the sporting stories of the year. Littler, don’t forget, is still a teenager. And that is what makes his supremacy all the more remarkable.

‌



Whatever your views on the sporting merits of darts, one thing is certain. Doing what Littler is doing takes mental fortitude of the highest order.

Gianni Infantino hits out at criticism as World Cup 2026 controversies glossed over READ MORE :

He has a sporting mentality that only the truly elite possess. He has been booed while on stage, his every move is scrutinised and documented, he is the player everyone wants to beat, and the player many people want to see beaten. Yet he remains focused, he remains unbeatable.

After the win at the World Matchplay in Blackpool, Littler has his sights set on an unprecedented clean sweep of the eight PDC (Professional Darts Corporation) ranking titles in the calendar year. He has the World Championship, the World Masters, the UK Open and the World Matchplay under his belt.

‌



The remaining four titles are the World Grand Prix, the European Championship, the Grand Slam of Darts and the Players Championship finals. The problem with the last of those is that Littler will have to qualify, which means playing in low-key Pro Tour events to accumulate prize money to finish in the top 64 in the rankings.

View 3 Images Luke Littler is now more than £2million ahead of Luke Humphries on the PDC order of merit (Image: Andrew Redington/Getty Images)

The 64th-placed player currently has £22,750 to his name. The irony, of course, is that Littler has now won more than £3million in two years, winning over £225,000 in Blackpool.

‌



But that does not count towards Players Championship rankings and Littler will now have to go and compete in some minor events in Leicester to try and qualify. That he is willing to do that is an insight into his sporting character.

Even at such an early stage of his career, Littler is driven by the record books and the history books. He was clearly very proud of beating two Phil Taylor records at the World Matchplay.

View 3 Images Luke Littler broke two of Phil Taylor's scoring records in his World Matchplay triumph (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

‌



Littler’s tournament average was 111.04, comfortably beating Taylor’s mark of 106.31 in 2010. And his average of 111.53 in the final against Price pipped Taylor’s 111.23 against Adrian Lewis in 2013.

On the PDC’s two-year order of merit system, Littler now has £3,143,500 to his name. That is £2.13million more than second-placed Luke Humphries.

Aside from that prize money, Littler has several lucrative commercial tie-ups, one of which will see him front a new Netflix show that will give 20 everyday darts players the chance to play against the world champion.

Article continues below

Heats will take place in Manchester and London before 20 players go through to the show, beat Luke Littler, and have a chance to win £501,000 if they do just that. They will need all the luck they can get.

Sports.title: PSG tell Liverpool outrageous Bradley Barcola transfer price as Chelsea cause problems
Sports.content:
PSG tell Liverpool outrageous Bradley Barcola transfer price as Chelsea cause problems

Liverpool's pursuit of PSG star Bradley Barcola this summer has been complicated by Chelsea

View 2 Images Liverpool have been told to pay £140m for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's hunt for a Mohamed Salah successor appears to have led them to the door of French attacker, Bradley Barcola. The winger, who impressed at this summer's World Cup, will not come cheap, however, with Chelsea inadvertently causing the Reds a major headache.

‌



The 23-year-old's club, Paris Saint-Germain, are reportedly demanding that any of Barcola's potential suitors cough up a stunning £145 million for his services. Their reasoning for such a steep fee is in response to the astonishing amounts Chelsea paid for Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers and Manchester City dished out for Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson this summer.

‌



According to French outlet Mercato, Barcola has indicated he wants to leave the reigning European champions. However, as the winger still has two years left on his contract, PSG believe that £140m is a fair reflection of his valuation, given his profile and the current market.

‌



Rogers recently joined Stamford Bridge outfit Chelsea for £117m, a British record, while his England team-mate, Anderson, has moved to the Etihad Stadium for £116m. The French publication adds that talks between Barcola and PSG over a new deal have now ceased, and there are no further discussions between the two parties.

PSG's price for Barcola would make him the third most expensive transfer in history. It would put him behind Neymar's move from Barcelona to PSG in 2017 for £200m and Kylian Mbappe's switch from Monaco to the Parisian giants in the same year for £165m.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Should Liverpool shell out such a sum, it would eclipse the £125m they paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak last summer. The Reds, now under Andoni Iraola, have made just one signing so far this transfer window.

Spanish World Cup winner Victor Munoz arrived from Osasuna for £34.5m, but he remains their sole addition so far. Speaking at his first press conference as Liverpool’s new head coach, Iraola admitted that his side needed more players.

He said: "Obviously we've signed two players already but we need more players – we know this. The club is working on this.

‌



"Me as a coach, selfishly, you want the players here [on] day one, ready to train from the pre-season, but we understand that football doesn't work like this. I know the club is working hard to get those signings and I'm trying obviously to help also."

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola's price tag has been set by PSG (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool striker Emile Heskey believes Barcola could prove a season-defining acquisition for the Reds. Heskey told BOYLE Sports: "Signing Bradley Barcola would be an amazing coup for Liverpool because he provides the pace and directness we've been missing on the left wing. We've been spoiled with Sadio Mané and Luis Díaz, and now we need Barcola to get the fans off their seats again."

‌



Former Man United and French forward Louis Saha believes Barcola possesses the qualities required to reach the pinnacle of the game.

Saha told Live Football Tickets: "Bradley Barcola is a terrific player. He has already won two Champions Leagues, and he could even win the World Cup over the next few weeks, his achievements for such a young player are staggering.

"He has enormous potential, and I'm not surprised Liverpool are looking at him. They need a replacement for Mohamed Salah, and Cody Gakpo has looked uncomfortable at times for them out wide. Barcola could easily fill either of those positions."

Sports.title: The 4 transfers Arsenal must complete for Mikel Arteta to win another Premier League title
Sports.content:
Arsenal ended an arduous 22-year wait for Premier League glory last term by winning the title under Mikel Arteta — and now they are hungry for continued domestic dominance.

The Gunners will be out to retain the title this year but know they cannot afford to stand still as their rivals strengthen across the board. Manchester City and Liverpool both have new managers who will want to make a strong impression, while Chelsea have already made some serious moves in the market.

Arsenal have made three signings so far (Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier and Piero Hincapie on a permanent) but are expected to push through far bigger deals before the transfer deadline.

The most eye-catching signing is likely to be the one that fills the left wing berth; Vinicius Junior is the latest player to be linked with Morgan Rogers now out of the equation and, with Arsenal wanting a real ceiling-raiser to level up their attack, the Real Madrid star certainly fits the bill in that respect. Whether or not a deal can be done in the next few weeks is another matter, particularly as it has been claimed Jose Mourinho wants to keep the Brazil international at the Bernabeu since news of Arsena's interest first emerged.

‌



Tzolis has already been signed from Club Brugge to replace the popular Leandro Trossard. As impressive as the Greece international's output was last season, he alone does not improve Arsenal's attack. That means they simply have to sign another left forward if they are to progress further this year — even if it means having to budge from their valuation of targets.

Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear READ MORE :

Bradley Barcola is another player who has been touted as a potential target but it seems as though Liverpool are pushing harder on that front right now. Yan Diomande, the other elite winger likely to move for big bucks this summer, seems to be Real Madrid bound. Arsenal reportedly enquired about Diomande last week. His prospective move to Real Madrid could, however, boost their chances of landing Vinicius Jr. So watch this space...

Central midfield is another area which is likely to see movement and Arsenal's pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes is in danger of becoming a bit of a saga. Arsenal want the Brazilian and he wants Arsenal. Unfortunately, Newcastle want their talismanic captain to stay put and are playing spoiler when it comes to a transfer.

As it transpired with Rogers, a move for Guimaraes will all come down to price; Newcastle will want a monster fee to sanction an exit and Arsenal will not want to pay what they deem silly money for a player who, although top-class, will turn 29 later this year. Suggestions last week were that Arsenal were ready to bid £70m for him. Subsequently, it was claimed Newcastle would reject that out of hand.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal's pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes is in danger of becoming a saga (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

If Guimaraes does prove to be unattainable, Arsenal are likely to turn their focus elsewhere. Alex Scott is well liked but again, Bournemouth don't want to sell and could demand in excess of £80m given the inflated transfer fees currently distorting the market. Ayyoub Bouaddi, one of the World Cup's breakout stars, is another player Arsenal have been linked with, although Manchester City are heavily courting the teenager amid speculation over Rodri's future.

With William Saliba out for the foreseeable future, Arsenal are also expected to add a centre-back. They have already set their sights on Ezri Konsa but, just as with Rogers prior to his Chelsea switch, their valuation of the player differs to that of Aston Villa. At 28 and coming off the back of a stellar World Cup with England, Konsa boasts Premier League pedigree and is versatile, too.

If Arsenal decide against pushing the boat out for Konsa, then his England team-mate, John Stones, is available on a free transfer and has the scope to be one of the bargains of the summer. Chelsea are also interested in the former Manchester City man, who has been doing his best to prevent Arsenal from winning the title in previous years. If the stars align before September 1, there's every chance he could be doing his bit to help them win it this time around.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal are also avid admirers of Julian Alvarez (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

If Arsenal do strengthen in those three positions, and depending on what sort of budget they have left available, there may be a chance they seek an elite centre-forward. That's despite spending significant money on Viktor Gyokeres last year.

Julian Alvarez is a player Arsenal have been linked with all the summer. He would command an absolutely seismic transfer fee, though, which would likely well eclipse the £125m that Liverpool parted with to sign Alexander Isak last year. He would represent an upgrade on Gyokeres, though, and it's even been suggested that Arsenal could offer the Swede as a makeweight to sweeten any prospective deal given Atletico Madrid do not want to sell Alvarez.

During his final season at Manchester City, Alvarez accumulated 21 goal contributions (11 goals, 10 assists) and is proven at Premier League level. A return to England may be unlikely, though, given Barcelona is thought to be the Argentina star's preferred destination.

Sports.title: Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits
Sports.content:
Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits

Manchester United have signed 19-year-old former Swansea City goalkeeper Kit Margetson and are looking to sell two other keepers in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Kit Margetson has joined Manchester United (Image: Poppy Townson/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have announced the signing of Kit Margetson as part of their overhaul of the goalkeeping department.

‌



Margetson, a Wales under-21 international, left Swansea City earlier this month when his contract expired. However, Swansea will receive a compensation fee for the young goalkeeper, having developed him since under-15 level under the eye of his father Martyn, who was until recently the Championship's side head of goalkeeping.

‌



He spent last season on loan at Connah's Quay Nomads where he made 34 appearances and kept 10 clean sheets. Margetson made his debut for Wales under-21s against Belarus in March.

‌



The club, who haven't announced the length of his contract, said in a statement: "Everyone at United would like to welcome Kit to the club and wish him the very best of luck for the future."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Margetson's arrival is the latest in a succession of moves in the goalkeeping department at Old Trafford. United signed Wales international Karl Darlow from Leeds on a free transfer to provide back-up to Senne Lammens, who himself only arrival last year.

‌



Previous No.1 Andre Onana has been loaned back to Turkish side Trabzonspor, while Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek are also set to depart in the coming weeks.

View 2 Images Radek Vitek could leave Manchester United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has greenlighted their departures to create space in the first-team squad. Bayindir has struggled to make an impact over the past few season and is seeking a permanent move, having not returned to United following the World Cup.

‌



Vitek spent last season on loan with Bristol City in the Championship and made a real impression. United are understood to value the the 22-year-old at £10million and have received plenty of interest in his services.

He started United's 5-0 pre-season win over Rosenborg on the weekend but will be allowed to leave, with Lammens and Darlow installed as the first and second-choice keepers and his value high after his Bristol City stint.

Sports.title: Arsenal will not be able to offer Vinicius Jr one thing he wants as huge update emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal will not be able to offer Vinicius Jr one thing he wants as huge update emerges

Vinicius Jr will be forced into a change should he join Arsenal from Real Madrid in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr is of interest to Arsenal this summer (Image: Michael Regan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Vinicius Jr would be denied his dream number at Arsenal if the Gunners were to clinch an extraordinary deal for the Real Madrid superstar. The 26-year-old emerged as a target for the Premier League side this past weekend.

‌



The Brazilian has spent eight years with the La Liga giants and with just 12 months left on his contract, rumours have circulated on whether his time at Madrid will come to an end. According to Diario AS, Vinicius hopes to continue at Madrid and optimism remains that a contract extension can be reached.

‌



However, if the winger does make the move to north London, he'll have to do without his favoured No. 7, having worn the number for the last three seasons in Spain. The jersey is currently occupied by Bukayo Saka, with Vinicius having to look elsewhere.

‌



Prior to receiving the storied jersey in 2023 upon the departure of Eden Hazard, the Brazilian had worn the No. 20 for three years, which is also unavailable at the Emirates Stadium, with Noni Madueke sporting the number.

Vinicius could revert back to the first two numbers he wore at Madrid - No. 28 and No. 25. Both jerseys are available in Mikel Arteta's squad, as well as No. 15 and No. 19 - the latter being vacated by Leandro Trossard's move to Besiktas.

Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move READ MORE :

While Vinicius won't be able to continue sporting No. 7 on the club stage if a move to Arsenal materialises, he will be able to call himself the most paid player in the club's history, according to reports.

‌



The Telegraph states that his staggering salary of £400,000 per week wouldn't stop the deal from happening. It further claims that club executives would aim to improve his wages to further convince the Brazilian to sign.

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr has 12 months left on his contract at Real Madrid (Image: Photo by Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

Vinicius' potential wages would easily usurp those of Arsenal's current highest-paid player, Saka. The England star inked a £365,000-a-week contract in February, which is set to rise each season.

The Brazil international is coming off his second-best goalscoring season in La Liga, with 16 goals scored. But he failed to win a major honour for a second season in a row at Madrid.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Newcastle agreement ‘days away’ as Bruno Guimaraes transfer talks accelerated
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Newcastle agreement ‘days away’ as Bruno Guimaraes transfer talks accelerated

Arsenal are pushing for a move for Newcastle United captain, Bruno Guimaraes, and plan to complete a deal with the Magpies in the coming days

View 2 Images Arsenal are eager to sign Bruno Guimaraes (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal are preparing to intensify talks with Newcastle United over Bruno Guimaraes, as they look to finally secure the Brazilian midfielder. It's been a lengthy saga between the two clubs this summer, with the Gunners keen on welcoming reinforcements to their engine room.

‌



That's despite the Magpies ultimately telling all interested parties that their captain is not for sale for any price. A shining light last season at St James' Park, Guimaraes has seen a wealth of attention in the current window.

‌



However, having already lost Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, Newcastle are eager to retain at least a portion of their foundation. Arsenal, however, have other ideas.

‌



Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes agent takes to social media as Arsenal prepare £70m bid for Newcastle star READ MORE :

It is understood that while no official discussions have begun, talkSPORT claim that Guimaraes has already reached an agreement on personal terms with the Gunners.

Andrea Berta's board are also reportedly prepared to offer at least £70million for the 28-year-old in the coming weeks, with sources additionally informing the publication that three verbal proposals have already been submitted by the North London club.

That's despite senior figures on Tyneside insisting that no official approach has been lodged as yet. Under contract until 2028, Newcastle are in no hurry to part with their captain, meaning they can essentially command whatever fee they desire to permit his departure.

‌



While Eddie Howe is determined to keep Guimaraes at the club ahead of the new campaign, the manager has conceded that the final decision ultimately lies beyond his control.

View 2 Images It looks to be a tough summer for Eddie Howe (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Speaking at the weekend, he said: "I've spoken to him as I would do. Bruno, normally, is just a fantastic person.

‌



"We've had some really good conversations, both before the World Cup, during the World Cup and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private.

"He's just a great player and a great person. Look, I don't know what's going to happen with Bruno's future.

"That's for other people to, one, speculate about, but also conversations that I'm not part of. We don't want to lose our best players.

‌



"That's an obvious statement to make. Losing those big two [Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali] is painful for us and difficult. For me, it's been another challenging summer so far."

Sports.title: F1 news: Lewis Hamilton controversy as star lashes out an 'unacceptable' incident
Sports.content:
F1 news: Lewis Hamilton controversy as star lashes out an 'unacceptable' incident

Lewis Hamilton was involved in a controversial moment during the Hungarian GP as one F1 star made his feelings clear about an incident on the track

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton was penalised during the Hungarian Grand Prix (Image: Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Lando Norris won the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday to claim his first victory of the campaign. The reigning world champion, who finished 15 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen, sits fifth in the drivers’ standings.

‌



Kimi Antonelli is currently leading the charge to take this year’s crown, having won six of 11 F1 races. Lewis Hamilton was denied the chance to shorten the Italian’s lead after receiving a controversial penalty for speeding in the pit lane.

‌



Meanwhile, Norris had battled his McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri for the lead during an early portion of the race. However, Piastri’s attempt to win was impacted by a collision with Carlos Sainz. Here is a round-up of some of the biggest F1 headlines following the Hungarian GP.

‌



Lewis Hamilton controversy

Sky Sports F1 pundit Anthony Davidson was left confused by Lewis Hamilton's penalty for pit lane speeding during the Hungarian Grand Prix. The incident occurred when Hamilton was travelling through the pit for his second change of tyres.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Race stewards stated that Hamilton had driven at 80.1kph in the pit lane, where the limit is 80kph. Consequently, he received a five-second time penalty, which dropped him to fifth place, having originally finished fourth but only four seconds ahead of his Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc. However, footage from above Hamilton's helmet appeared to show him pressing his pit limiter button at the right time.

‌



Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton set to make first UK appearance at Ethnicity Awards READ MORE :

F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges READ MORE :

"I've looked at this so many times and I can't work out why he gets a penalty,” Davidson said during the Sky Sports broadcast. “For me, he slows down sufficiently well. We've got this marker board on the left-hand side that stipulates the 80kph speed limit. I don't see that [speeding].

"Let's have a look at the exit. Obviously knew he was under time pressure to get out in that race with [Kimi] Antonelli. Again, for me, it sounds like he releases the pit lane button on the line itself. This guy knows what he's doing when it comes to white lines and when to press the button.

"Maybe there was just an error when he was a bit too close to the line on the actual speed of the car and they were just pinged by that. Who knows? Strange that it only happened that one time. I don't have enough data here and I can only go by the sound of when he is pressing that button. For me, it looked totally fine on the way in and on the way out."

‌



View 2 Images McLaren driver Oscar Piastri spoke out after the Hungarian GP (Image: Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Oscar Piastri on ‘unacceptable’ incident

Oscar Piastri hit out at Carlos Sainz for colliding with him during the Hungarian GP. The McLaren driver was battling teammate Lando Norris for the lead when he approached Sainz and Fernando Alonso, who were both a lap down.

Sainz attempted to overtake Alonso but failed to complete the move before cutting across Piastri’s path, which led to a collision. Stewards deemed Sainz responsible for the crash on lap 39, with the Williams driver receiving a five-second penalty, while Piastri ultimately did not finish the race due to a gearbox failure.

Article continues below

"I couldn't believe what happened," Piastri said. "Getting crashed into by a lapped car is never one of the things you expect that can go wrong in your race. And today it was.

"I don't really care if he didn't see me and the fact that he didn't and no one told him, or there was a lack of complete awareness, is unacceptable."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
